jobs.title: Install the Chief relay on the Mini
jobs.body:
Install the Chief relay on the Mini (Ben asked for it, 7 Oct; AGENTS.md "Chief relay"). Free; nothing on YouTube.

    cd ~/YouTube/orbit-with-ben && git pull
    mkdir -p ~/_desk/bin ~/_desk/state && cp scripts/chief_relay.py ~/_desk/bin/
    cp scripts/mini/com.owb.chief-relay.plist ~/Library/LaunchAgents/
    launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.owb.chief-relay.plist
    python3 ~/_desk/bin/chief_relay.py status

Then check, and put each result in the done note:
- `status` shows Cursor UP and, if Codex is installed, Codex UP. Grok shows down until it runs jobs.py.
- `codex exec --help` lists `--full-auto`, `--add-dir` and `-c`. If a flag is missing, set CODEX_FLAGS in the plist
  (an EnvironmentVariables dict) to what this version accepts, and say what you set.
- If a ~/_desk/state/cursor-covers-chief file exists from the old worker, delete it. It does nothing now.
- After the first run, the end of ~/Library/Logs/chief-relay.log.
jobs.result: Relay installed and running (launchd com.owb.chief-relay, pid 59393, first run 13:08 woke Cursor); ~/_desk/bin script and LaunchAgents plist match the repo. status: Grok down (no heartbeat), Cursor UP, Codex UP. Codex 0.160.0 has no --full-auto: installed plist now sets CODEX_FLAGS='exec -s workspace-write --approve-for-me -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true --add-dir "<HOS>" --add-dir ~/_desk'. Also set CODEX_BIN=~/.npm-global/bin/codex (launchd's zsh -lc PATH missed it: log said codex 'CLI not installed') and HOS_REPO='~/YouTube/History Of Science' (default history-of-science doesn't exist). Same three via launchctl setenv so they apply without a reload. Old cursor-covers-chief deleted. Log tail: chain chief=down | cursor=UP | codex=down (CLI not installed) [pre-fix]; run: cursor (cap 1500s).

jobs.title: Gemini: Sun 022 pictures vs words, and the clock numbers
jobs.body:
Gemini (agy) check of the Sun 022 pictures and graphic numbers, before the first cut's review pack (Fri 9 Oct).
No spend. Don't edit the shot list or the script; report only.

1. Picture vs words. For every GODDARD and NASA row in 02_Video-Projects/022_Is-the-Sun-Getting-Brighter/07_Edit-Project/shot_list_v01.csv:
   open the source page (svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/<id> for SVS ids; images.nasa.gov or the NASA page for the rest) and record
   what it really shows: instrument, wavelength, date, and whether it is a real observation or a visualisation.
   Flag any row where the VO line at that moment says something the picture isn't, for example "flare" over a
   prominence, today's Sun under a line about the young Sun, or a simulation shown as if it were film.
2. Numbers in the code graphics. clocks.mp4 (row 96) draws three clocks: about 1% per 110 million years; about 0.1% up
   and down over the 11-year cycle; a prominence lasting about a day. Check each one against 01_Script/SOURCES.md and
   the primary source, with the exact quote.
3. Write 07_Edit-Project/GEMINI_PICTURE_CHECK_v01.md: one table row per flagged shot (row, id, what it shows, the VO
   line, why it's wrong, a suggested swap from the row's fallback or NASA_POOL_v01.md), then the clock numbers, then
   "all other rows OK" with the count. Commit it and mark the job done with the commit.
Claude decides every swap.

jobs.title: 024: full rough v02 (Claude v01 review: 5 assembler fixes)
jobs.body:
Claude review of 024 full_rough_v01 (pack b758d7e): FAIL, with 5 fixes, all assembler-only. Write `_assemble_light_speed_full_v02.py` from v01, re-render, and post `full_rough_v02_pack`.

1. **Frame 0 is too dim and too still.** frame0_sheet shows sparse grey dots with no visible motion by 1 s. Start row 1 from the part of `starfield` where the field is crowding forward and blue (about 12 s or later in the render, like the 261 s and 294 s frames). The frame0 sheet must show the motion by 1 s.
2. **Corner bug in frame.** The "Earth from the Space Station" logo is visible top-left in the NHQ_2019_0626 spans at 247.3, 422.9, 430.5 and 436.8 s. Crop past it (upscale ≤2.35×) or use a span or still without it. No text in frame.
3. **Row 23: swap `sts33-17-005a`.** It's a close-up portrait of Manley "Sonny" Carter, who died in 1991. Don't use a named astronaut's face as generic B-roll. Use `iss019e018483` (Expedition 19, crew at work) or another NASA ISS interior where no single face is the subject.
4. **Rows 27/28: the 1.82 s `iss035e017673` cut.** Drop it. Start the row 28 DC-8 shot at the 317.05 s pause, slightly ahead of its line.
5. **Rows 38–39 end on 7 starfield jump cuts** (461–491 s). Different offsets of one render read as glitches, not cuts.
   - Row 38: end on the ISS dawn limb, holding it to 464.98 s. Drop the starfield cut at 461.4.
   - Row 39: render `starfield --seconds 27` and play it **continuously** from 464.98 s to the end (VO out at 487.54, then the 2.5 s hold and 1 s fade), with a slow push-in and **no cuts**. The 6 s cap is waived for this bookend return only, as with the Venus Maat Mons bookends.

Unchanged and passing:
- Omni trims.
- The reuse cap.
- Upscale (2.1× max).
- Cuts in pauses.
- -14.3 LUFS.
- Chapter cards.
- Black Marble used in edit only.

Re-run clip_check and align, and include the frame0 and end sheets.

jobs.title: 025: full rough v02 (every frame fills 16:9, drop text/annotated plates, push on static holds, rows 28/30, sheets)
jobs.body:
Claude on 025 full rough v01 (58e441f). Build v02 with these fixes and post `full_rough_v02_pack`. **Force-add the sheets this time:** the v01 commit has no `frames/row_###.jpg`, `per_row_sheet`, frame0, 0–8 s, end or Omni sheets, so Claude can't review the picture.

1. **Open and bookend panorama (PIA22909): take option (a).**
   - Tighten the pan window to the filled band so no black mosaic gap or grey tile is ever in frame, at upscale ≤2.35× (asserted).
   - Keep it panning from frame 0, and keep the row 32 bookend the same pan, further along.
   - If the filled band can't give a clean 16:9 at ≤2.35×, use option (b): a fully filled ground-level Mars panorama from the pool for **both** the open and the bookend. Never a whole globe.
2. **Static holds.** Give each a slow push or pan (3–6% over the shot): cut 64 (row 21, PIA22520), cut 96 (row 28, PIA25739) and the 1 s freeze at 26.9 s (row 5, PIA25739). Re-run freezedetect and get 0 freezes over 0.8 s.
3. **Rows 28 and 30 WARN.** Move those cuts to the nearest sentence-end pause (≥0.25 s) within ±1.5 s. If there's none, keep them between words and list them in the pack.
4. Everything else stays as v01: Omni spans, reuse ≤2, cuts in pauses, -14.3 LUFS, the hold and fade.

5. **Every frame fills 16:9 (Claude's full review of the v01 sheets in b3d987a).** v01 has many raw mosaics with black or white jagged edges, split panels and tilted strips.
   - **The fix:** for each plate, crop into its filled area at ≤2.35×. If that can't fill the frame, swap in another ground-level plate from the pool.
   - **Add a fill gate to the assembler** and report it in the pack: fail any row frame whose near-black (<12) or near-white (>245) pixels touching the border cover over 1.5% of the frame.
   - Seen in v01:
     - **Mosaic edges:** PIA22909, PIA07372, PIA17759, PIA07371, PIA01907, PIA21717, PIA10128, PIA16096, PIA26559, PIA25176, PIA12142, PIA12203, PIA26237, PIA26236 and PIA20328.
     - **Tilted strip:** PIA12102, which should be dropped.
     - **Split panels:** PIA00382 and PIA07458. Use one panel only, or drop them.
6. **Drop plates with text or annotations.** There's no text in frame except the house chapter cards:
   - PIA12338 (the "July 2009 / August 2009" labels);
   - PIA22520 (the "June 10" label; both uses);
   - PIA26482 (the "Hard Landing" infographic);
   - PIA12490 (green box annotation);
   - PIA24270 (inset box; crop to the main view if that clears it at ≤2.35×, else drop).
7. **Drop PIA25739 (rows 5 and 28).** It reads as a blank grey-lilac frame. Use a ground-level dayscape instead.
8. **Keep, but no longer than 3 s:** PIA22929, Opportunity's last image, which is noisy but is the story at row 21. PIA12337 (JPL's reconstruction of Spirit at Troy) stays: it's a NASA illustration and reads as one.

Render detached and post the pack.

jobs.title: 025 Mars robot: Ben's notes, swap the 2:54 image + 025's own music bed (v03d + phone copy)
jobs.body:
**Ben's notes on 025 v03c (board tick, 8 Oct 22:39).** He wants two changes. Make **v03d** from the v03c build, and change nothing else.

1. **2:54 "This image looks bad."** That's cut 39, row 14, 170.73–175.97 s: PIA12337, the CAD "Computer Reconstruction of Spirit Predicament". It's a flat brown background, 1094 px wide and upscaled 1.84×.
   - Replace it with **PIA12102**, "Spirit Photographs Her Underbelly, Sol 1925". It's a real photo of the stuck wheels and isn't used anywhere else in the cut.
   - If PIA12102 can't fill 16:9 at an upscale of 2.35× or less, use **PIA12205** (HiRISE, "Orbital View of Spirit at Troy").
   - Same timing; still_motion push; jitter ≤ 0.35 px; fill and polish gates PASS for the new cut. Drop PIA12337 from the long.
2. **"Are we sure we have not used this background music before?"** Ben's right. v03c's bed is `OWB UAT/jupiter-music.mp3`, the same bed the 023 and 024 cuts use. Every earlier film (013, 021, 022) had its own `<film>_score_bed_v01`.
   - Make 025's own bed with `04_Audio/tools/generate_music_bed.py` (ElevenLabs API; no website generation): `--project mars-robot --length-ms 500000 --out-dir 02_Video-Projects/025_Could-A-Robot-Survive-On-Mars/05_Music`.
   - Prompt (pass as `--prompt`): "Instrumental cinematic space documentary underscore for Orbit with Ben, Mars robot film. Cold dusty red plains and a small machine that refuses to stop: lonely, patient, quietly brave, with a slow ache as the power fades. Soft low strings, muted felt piano, warm analog pads, sparse mechanical ticks kept very quiet, thin wind texture. NOT Jupiter music, NOT Saturn ring chimes, NOT Moon Leaving lunar piano, NOT Sun golden strings. Vast quiet scale, room for British narration. Pace: 60-72 BPM, slow and steady under the narration, the low strings lifting only for the Opportunity farewell. No vocals, no drums, no EDM, no trailer hit."
   - **Credit guard.** Read ElevenLabs credits left first. Don't generate if fewer than 30,000 would be left afterwards (voice work comes first). Instead, block this job with "music bed: needs Claude's call on credits".
   - After generating, record credits before and after in `04_Audio/elevenlabs_ledger.jsonl` (stem `mars-robot_score_bed_v01`). One generation only. If it sounds wrong, post it; don't re-roll.
   - Mix exactly as v03c (≈ −14 LUFS, bed under the VO, music for the full runtime, fade at the end).
3. **Deliver:**
   - `OWB UAT/025_MarsRobot_full_rough_v03d.mp4`;
   - **`OWB UAT/025_MarsRobot_v03d_PHONE.mp4`**, the same phone encode as J0067 (it's the file Ben opens), and confirm it's uploaded;
   - a pack with the new cut's frame and the gates.
4. Post on #99 for Claude's check. Don't delete or move anything in OWB UAT.

5. **The new checks (AGENTS.md lesson 7, Ben 8 Oct)** run on v03d, with both reports in the pack:
   - `python3 scripts/picture_qa.py <v03d.mp4> --cuts cuts_v03d.json --pool nasa_pool_v01.json --out-dir <pack>` must PASS;
   - `python3 scripts/music_gate.py 02_Video-Projects/025_Could-A-Robot-Survive-On-Mars --bed <bed> --video <v03d.mp4> --out <pack>/music_gate.json` must PASS.
   - **Calibration, once:** run music_gate's `similarity()` on every pair of real beds on the Mini (`jupiter-music.mp3`, 013's, 021's, 022's and the new 025 bed), and post the matrix. Two different real beds should score under 0.8.

6. **Codex's picture ideas (#6071491327), accepted by Claude.** Picture only: the VO stays locked, and the same gates run.
   a. **Opening (0–5.67 s, row 1):** the first sentence is about Opportunity, but the shot is bare ground. Use a verified real Opportunity picture that shows the rover itself: its own deck with the solar panels, its shadow on Mars, or a HiRISE view of it. Not an artist's concept. Fill 16:9, no Orbit at frame 0. Update `frame0_sheet`.
   b. **Name labels:** the first time each machine appears (Opportunity, Spirit, Phoenix, InSight, Curiosity, Ingenuity), add a small lower-left name in the house font for about 2.5 s. White, soft shadow, no box, off the subject. Nothing else on screen.
   c. **One machine per passage:** where the narration follows one machine, every picture in that passage shows that machine or its own view. List any cut that shows a different rover. Swap it only for a verified same-machine picture from the pool (reuse ≤ 2). If none exists, leave it and say so.
   d. **Wheel holes (359.9–364.3 s):** hold the real puncture photo through the whole "holes … punching through" sentence, and move Orbit's existing reaction to just after it. Shift timings only; no new clip.
   e. **Panel cleaning:** only if the NASA images API has a verified before/after pair from the same rover (same camera, matching view), crop them to match and time the change to the cleaning sentence. Otherwise skip, and give the IDs you checked.

**Where viewers leave each long (Claude, 8 Oct).** The longs' average viewed is 2–26% (Moon 1.7%, Neutron 2.9%, Alien Worlds 4.1%), so most viewers leave in the first seconds. The tracker has no retention curve, so we can't see where they leave.

jobs.title: 026 Nearest Star: its own score bed (Claude's brief, credit guard)
jobs.body:
**026's own score bed (AGENTS.md lesson 7). Claude wrote the brief from the script.** The VO runs about 494 s, so ask for the full runtime.

Run `04_Audio/tools/generate_music_bed.py --project nearest-star --length-ms 520000 --out-dir 02_Video-Projects/026_How-Far-Is-The-Nearest-Star/05_Music --generate --prompt "<below>"`:

"Instrumental cinematic space documentary underscore for Orbit with Ben, Nearest Star film. Night-sky wonder and quiet curiosity: the hush of looking up on a clear night, then the dizzying scale of the gap between the stars, then a long patient journey outward. Glassy celesta and soft bell tones, airy synth pads, gentle pulsing low strings, a slow-building warm string swell for the scale reveal, a hopeful lift near the end, closing on a long held chord. Pace: 66-80 BPM, steady and unhurried under British narration. NOT Jupiter music, NOT Saturn ring chimes, NOT Moon Leaving lunar piano, NOT Sun golden strings, NOT the Mars robot's lonely felt piano and low strings. No vocals, no choir words, no drums, no EDM, no trailer hit."

**Rules:**
- **Credit guard:** read ElevenLabs credits left first. Don't generate if fewer than 30,000 would be left afterwards. Expect about 7,000 credits for 520 s.
- **If the API returns short:** follow 025's method. Make one continuation take with the same prompt plus "Continuation of the same piece: same key, tempo and instrumentation", and join the takes with an 8 s equal-power crossfade at a chapter break. Never more than two takes, and never loop.
- **Check:** `music_gate.py` on the bed must PASS (own, brief, not reused, no gap).
- **Log:** both takes go in the ledger.
- **Post:** the bed, its gate result and the credits.

jobs.body:

  - row 11 air 8–14 s: `--label "the air keeps going" --label2 "faster than sound"`.

  - row 20 dayyear: `--label "1 day = 1 year"`.
  - row 25 tides: `--label "4 cm a year"` (the VO says about four centimetres).
  - row 30 clock: `--label "22 hours"` only (Claude #6082954189).
  - row 33 clock: no labels.
  - row 35 speed and tides: no labels.

**Claude #6081907573 (9 Oct):** re-render the six globe graphics with the real-Earth `globe()` (f6b2c93). Download blue_marble.jpg once (curl in the docstring), and Pillow is needed. Row 22: Mariner 10 Venus only. Row 34: USGS Kīlauea lava → Blue Marble oceans → IceBridge Greenland melt, cut to 'molten core / oceans / melting ice'.

**Build from `07_Edit-Project/SHOT_LIST_v02.md` (Claude, 9 Oct): the sudden-stop chapter moves up, the agenda line is cut, and the first answer comes at about 24 s.** v01 rows keep their pictures except where v02 says otherwise.

**027 Earth Stopped Spinning: picture, rough v01 (Claude, 9 Oct).** Build it from `07_Edit-Project/SHOT_LIST_v01.md` and `code_graphics.py`, to the same standard as 026.

Everything 026 needed four cuts to learn applies from the start:
- **Frame 0** is real, moving footage (DSCOVR EPIC or the ISS terminator). No fade, no title.
- **No labels or burnt-in text** in any frame. Check every frame of video clips, not just the first: ESO and NASA videos often draw labels in partway through.
- **No insets**, meaning no picture boxed over another picture. A subject picture always runs full frame.
- **Reuse:** a still or a time-lapse at most twice, counted by file. A code graphic may be used 3 times only if its state moves each time.
- **Upscale ≤ 2.35×.** Fetch the largest copy first; ESA/Hubble wallpapers often go to 2048 px.
- **Crops:** no crop runs past the picture edge (026's pillarbox strip). All-sky or panorama plates are cropped tight to 16:9.
- **Video clips:** use only parts that are neither black (fade-ins) nor labelled.
- **Render scratch:** keep current + previous only (AGENTS.md).

**Spend:** the 2 Omni beats and 2 Veo Fast props are on free Vertex only, with the £5 floor (£22.51 left). If one would cross the floor, use the shot list's £0 fallback and say so.

**Music:** 027's own bed waits for the ElevenLabs renewal on 30 Oct. Cut to the VO with no bed for now; the score is laid in after 30 Oct.

**Gates:** picture_qa with the pool, polish_gate, clip_check and the fill gate (WARN). Pack the per-row sheet, frame0_sheet and picture_qa_review for Claude.

jobs.body:
**023's own score bed (AGENTS.md lesson 7). Claude wrote the brief from the script.** Ask for the full runtime: the VO cut runs 513 s.

"Instrumental cinematic space documentary underscore for Orbit with Ben, Venus film. A mystery about a lost twin: calm curiosity at first, then a slow, heavy, smothering heat as the greenhouse story unfolds, a dim orange evening that never ends, then a reflective close about how lucky Earth is. Warm low drones, slow bowed cello and viola, muted brass swells far in the distance, soft heat-shimmer textures, a gentle rise for the runaway-greenhouse reveal, ending on a held unresolved chord. NOT Jupiter music, NOT Saturn ring chimes, NOT Moon Leaving lunar piano, NOT Sun golden strings, NOT the Mars robot's lonely felt piano and low strings, NOT the Nearest Star's glassy celesta and bells. No vocals, no choir words, no drums, no EDM, no trailer hit."

jobs.title: 026 Nearest Star: Ben's fixes, two graphics + Orbit's two scenes back in (v05)
jobs.body:
**Ben's fixes for 026 (board, 9 Oct 08:44Z): two graphics don't show what the narration says.**

**1. At 1:48–1:52 (row 9, `journey`).** The VO says: *"A light-year is a distance, not a time. It is how far light travels in a year. So when you look towards Proxima, you are seeing light that left it more than four years ago."* The cut shows `journey`, the three-line walk/car/jet race, which belongs to row 24. The shot list asked for a single light streak from Proxima to Earth.
- **New code graphic `lightyear`, text-free, about 8 s:** Proxima (the red-dwarf glow the code graphics already use) on the left and a small blue Earth on the right, across a full-frame star field.
- One bright pulse of light leaves Proxima and travels to Earth. Four and a quarter evenly spaced tick marks along the path light up as it passes them, one tick per year. The pulse arrives on "light that left it more than four years ago".
- No labels or numbers, no boxed panel. It replaces only the `journey` cut at row 9, so `journey` drops to 2 uses.

**2. At 6:02–6:18 (row 27, `lighttimes`).** The VO says: *"Moonlight reaches you in just over a second. Sunlight takes about eight minutes. Light from the nearest star takes more than four years, and that is the shortest trip of its kind there is."* Bars on a log scale read as a chart; a viewer can't tell what they are. Make it an example instead of a graph.
- **New code graphic `lightrace`, text-free, timed to each sentence:** a small real-photo Earth disc on the right, and on the left, in turn, the real source as a cut-out disc on black space (no box):
  - the Moon (`GSFC_20171208_Archive_e001982`, its 2nd use);
  - the Sun (`GSFC_20171208_Archive_e002035`, its 2nd use);

jobs.title: 023 Venus v05d: Ben's 4 notes (diagrams at 1:22, 4:02, 5:38; Pioneer probe at 3:55)
jobs.body:
**J0095 is done (Claude, 63eabdd): the new graphics and their row timings.** Stills: `code_graphics_v02_stills_claude.jpg`.
- Download once, next to `code_graphics.py` (both out of git): `venus_disc.jpg` = https://images-assets.nasa.gov/image/PIA23791/PIA23791~orig.jpg and `blue_marble.jpg` (the same file as 027's). Pillow is needed. Labels use Arial Bold.
- **Rows 13c + 14a + 14b (78.2–96.3 s): one `albedo` clip, 18.1 s.** It replaces 14b's PIA00104, because the "soaks up less" payoff lands on 14b's words.
- **Row 31 (236.2–247.1 s): new `heavyh`, 10.9 s.**
- **Rows 32a + 32b (247.1–260.4 s): one `deuterium` clip, 13.3 s.** It replaces 32b's PIA00257. Row 32c stays.
- Render at those exact lengths (`--seconds`), at offset 0 each, with no freeze-padding. The beats are timed to the voice inside each clip.

**Ben's v05c notes (board, 9 Oct 13:36Z), 023 Venus → v05d.** New AGENTS rule (c5660ec): a code graphic must read with the sound off.

1. **1:22 (rows 13c/14a, `albedo`): "Need to make these animated diagrams better."** Claude is redrawing `albedo` in `code_graphics.py` (the companion Claude job): real Venus and Earth discs, labels, and bars that say what they are. Re-render once that lands.
2. **3:55 (row 30b, ARC-1978-AC78-9245): "Multiple probes, can we fact check this?"** The fact checks out. Pioneer Venus Multiprobe (9 Dec 1978) dropped four probes: one large and three small. The heavy-hydrogen reading came from the **Large Probe's** mass spectrometer (Donahue et al. 1982, Science 216, 630). The VO's "a NASA probe" is right, but the painting shows all four. Fix: reframe both 9245 spans in 30b on the **large probe alone** (push in so the three small probes are out of frame). If the crop goes soft at 1080p, use the NSSDCA/NASA Ames image of the Pioneer Venus Large Probe instead.
3. **4:02 (rows 31/32a, `deuterium`): "Animated diagram hard to understand."** Claude is redrawing `deuterium` too. Re-render once it lands.
4. **5:38 (rows 39a/39b): "Same with this one."**
   - **39a** (split, ocean world | steam lid): put a short label under each half from the line, "Way 2016: shallow oceans" | "Turbet 2021: a lid of steam", in house type at 4 words or fewer. Keep the slow push.

jobs.title: 025 Mars Short length test: one 50–60 s Short lifted from locked long Js6EQJ8qDi8, private-scheduled Thu 12 Nov 11:30 London (Chief-OK'd one-off; lowest priority)
jobs.body:
**Short length test, Chief OK 11 Oct 2026. A one-off exception to the 22–27 s lock** (AGENTS.md → *Packaging*). Astrum's Shorts mostly run 55–80 s and ours run 22–27 s. One 50–60 s Orbit Short goes out alongside the usual three that week, and the numbers decide.

- **Source: the locked 025 long, `Js6EQJ8qDi8`** (`02_Video-Projects/025_Could-A-Robot-Survive-On-Mars/09_Final-Export/025_MarsRobot_full_rough_v03f.mp4`, sha256 `cce6268c…` in UPLOADS.json). It's uploaded, and the file on an id is never swapped, so this picture and VO are final.
  - Lift one self-contained 50–60 s stretch of its VO and picture, and reframe it to 9:16 the way the house Shorts do.
  - **Spend nothing:** no new VO, no new picture generation, no new music bed (use the long's laid bed). The house SFX kit is fine.
  - Pick a story that isn't the main subject of that week's three Shorts: Mon 9 Nov `iyvWYFP_ETA`, Wed 11 Nov `TtgHNLXfDSs`, Fri 13 Nov `bSjWiCbB7pY` (Ingenuity). For example, Opportunity's 90 days → 14 years and the 2018 storm, if the long covers it.
- **Slot: Thu 12 Nov 2026, 11:30 London (11:30Z).** It's the only Short that day, after the four-week test (ends 6 Nov), with the long already public (Sun 8 Nov 18:00).
- **Every other Short rule still applies:**
  - the six opening rules: the named thing at frame 0, moving, no Orbit, the frame-0 whoosh, the 2–4 word hook caption;
  - the exact long title on screen at 9–14 s;
  - captions throughout;
  - the last 4 s loop to the open;
  - the Polish pass Short items (SFX level PASS, grain);
  - a custom cover (§4).
  - The title is new, in one of the six shapes, and not a copy of an existing one (Chief OKs it).
- **Gate:** `python3 00_Brand/Channel-Setup/tools/gate_shorts_open.py check <mp4> --air-date 2026-11-12 --length-test` must PASS (band 50–60 s, FAIL at 61 s; frame 0 distinct from Mon/Wed/Fri). Also `sfx_kit.py level`.
- **Review:** post the cut path, a contact sheet and the gate output on #99, then run `jobs.py block <this id> --agent <you> --reason "parked for Chief: final OK" --git`.
- **After the Chief's OK:** upload Private with publishAt `2026-11-12T11:30:00Z` through `youtube:package` (it mirrors Buffer at the same time). Set the cover in Studio (CDP 9223), and register it in UPLOADS.json with `"lengthTest": true`. Then run `gate_shorts_open.py add`. Related → `Js6EQJ8qDi8` is a separate job, after the long is public.
- **Priority:** lowest. It yields to every 024–027 focus job and never delays a locked schedule. It must be uploaded by Tue 10 Nov. If it can't make that, block with the reason and the slot is dropped (no rescheduling into another Short's day).
- **Measure:** the Orbit Auditor logs it against the week's three 22–27 s Shorts in its next numbers report, in `00_Brand/Channel-Setup/audits/SHORT_LENGTH_TEST_2026-11/TEST_LOG.md`.

jobs.body:
**No-cover-text Test & Compare (Reference lessons 5a, Chief OK 11 Oct 2026). A test, not a rule change.** SEA's two fastest longs have no cover text at all. One Orbit long tests the same idea.

- **Long: JWST `ziKBPJ6FY0U`** (*JWST Found Galaxies That Shouldn't Exist Yet*). The glowing galaxies are already the hook, and no Test & Compare is on record for it.
  - Not one of the five J0133 longs, nor Moon `2fsQcea-voM` or Alien Worlds `b8-X_FyJnHM` (J0099 tests running), Mars `Js6EQJ8qDi8` or Sun `h8HGfyShEHI` (A/B/C set).
  - **Fallback: Jupiter `-jmMROGoZCM`.** Use it only if Studio shows a test already running on JWST. If both have one, block with the reason. Never press Continue on "Run a new test?".
- **Build B** = the live thumb's plate with **no text at all**, same crop and grade.
  - Rebuild it from the clean plate (the builder under `00_Brand/Channel-Setup/tools/` or the film's `08_Thumbnail/`).
  - Never inpaint text away with an image model, and spend nothing. If no clean plate exists, block with "parked for Chief: no clean plate".
  - Save the live thumb as A (`https://i.ytimg.com/vi/<id>/maxresdefault.jpg`) to `~/_desk/notext_tc_1011/` with sha256 values, for rollback.
  - `thumb_preview.py long <A> <B> --out <sheet> --score` (B gets no text-size check).
- **Review:** post the A/B sheet and the score lines on #99, then run `jobs.py block <this id> --agent <you> --reason "parked for Chief: no-text T&C review" --git`.
- **After the Chief's OK:** in Orbit Studio (CDP 9223; check the channel is `UC_esArsDKd3GJvOkeO0DUog`), open Test & Compare, choose **Thumbnail only**, and set A = live and B = no-text.
  - Image-only inputs. Don't touch the title, schedule or privacy.
  - Reload, and confirm "Running…".
  - Record it in `00_Brand/Channel-Setup/audits/THUMB_AUDIT_2026-10-09/notext_test_compare.json`, like `j0099_test_compare.json`.
- **Read:** past about 500 impressions, or when YouTube names a winner. The Orbit Auditor reports it. The yellow-word rule stands until Chief changes it in AGENTS.md.
- **Done:** post a [Cursor] note on #99 with the id, the variants and the result.

**026 Nearest Star Shorts: Orbit Desk test (Chief OK, 12 Oct 2026). Assembly level only. No VO, picture or credit spend.**
Source: Orbit Creator's pack `026_shorts_pack_v01.md` (read on main `90f223f`). Shorts: `10_Shorts/mon16_cant_see_nearest_star`, `wed18_robot_reach_nearest_star`, `fri20_grapefruit_cherry` (Mon 16 / Wed 18 / Fri 20 Nov, 11:30 London).

**DEPENDENCY: don't render until the 026 long has a real upload id.** The long (`How Far Is the Nearest Star?`, Sun 15 Nov 18:00) isn't uploaded yet, and no upload job exists. This job is held (blocked) until it has an id in UPLOADS.json / the upload result; Chief reopens it then. Never render a card with a placeholder id.

1. **Titles (listing and on-screen):**
   - Mon: "If You Can't See the Nearest Star, How Far Away Is It?"
   - Wed: "If Voyager Needs 75,000 Years, How Far Is the Nearest Star?"
   - Fri: "The Nearest Star Is a Cherry Past Cairo. How Do We Know?"
   These replace Claude's 6 Oct titles. The on-screen title at 9–14 s must match the listing title exactly.
2. **End card, over the last ~4 s.** It holds at least 2 s past the last VO word and stays readable through the final frame. Contents: the long's thumb A (`08_Thumbnail/abc_v01/nearest_star_thumb_A_you-cant-see-it.jpg`, "YOU CAN'T SEE IT", unaltered), the exact long title `How Far Is the Nearest Star?` in white, and the long's real upload id in yellow. All of it sits inside the 16:9 centre band (layout in pack §1.3). No Orbit.
   Quote line, word for word from the long's VO:
   - Mon: "Your two eyes are a ruler." (long VO ~2:21)
   - Wed: "Could we ever go and look?" (~7:00)
   - Fri: a small "VOYAGER" label above "It has barely left the town." (~5:10)
3. **Loop exception (Chief OK, 12 Oct):** on these three Shorts only, the end card replaces the last-3-s loop back to the open. The loop rule stands everywhere else.
4. **VO stays locked** (`_vo_v01_LOCK`): no re-voicing, no new VO line, **no trim on Wed** (its take is 21.60 s; a trim would break 22 s). The Wed myth-bust at ~0:11–0:15 is logged as soft borderline, not FAIL.
5. **026 long: no Studio Test & Compare during its Shorts week**, so the long shows thumb A, matching the card. (Thumb testing stays on 024.)

**Pass conditions (Orbit Auditor's checks):**
- each card quote's timestamp measured in the final long cut, not the VO file; any moved quote logged with its new time;
- every Short runs 22 s or more (locked takes Mon 24.48, Wed 21.60, Fri 20.64 s; Wed and Fri clear 22 s only through the end-card hold);
- the on-screen title at 9–14 s matches the listing title exactly;
- the card shows thumb A, the exact long title, a yellow id from the real upload, and the Fri "VOYAGER" label.
Measure: the 026 long's day-7 views against Mars (025). Mars week stays unchanged as the control.

jobs.title: 030 Apophis Short: DATA scale bar overlay 32,000 vs 36,000 KM (split from J0223)
jobs.body:
**030 Apophis standalone Short: the one DATA overlay (split from J0223, kind `chart`).** SCRIPT_v01 visual must, `02_Video-Projects/030_Apophis-Closer-Than-Our-Satellites/10_Shorts/standalone_apophis/SCRIPT_v01.md`.

- **What:** a scale bar. Our own real-body Earth (Blue Marble crop, never a flat disc) at the bottom of the band; a thin satellite ring arc above it labelled **36,000 KM**; the rock's path drawing in *under* the ring, labelled **32,000 KM**. One idea: the rock passes inside the satellite ring.
- **Numbers (MUST QUOTE, NASA Apophis Facts, SCRIPT_v01 row A2):** 32,000 km from the surface; geosynchronous satellites ~36,000 km altitude. Labels exactly "36,000 KM" and "32,000 KM" (UK captions; KM in caps is fine).
- **Render:** one transparent overlay clip for its own row, `code_graphic_030short_r05_scale_v01.mov` (ProRes 4444 with alpha, 1080×1920, 30 fps, **3.6 s**), plus a PNG still of its fully built frame. Put the script at `10_Shorts/standalone_apophis/_build_code_graphic_scale_v01.py` and the render in `10_Shorts/standalone_apophis/code_graphics_v01/` (media is git-ignored).
- **Timing inside the clip:** 0–0.4 s Earth + ring fade/slide in; at **0.5 s** the "36,000 KM" label ticks in (the assembler lands this on the spoken "36,000", raw VO 18.58 s, earlier after pause trim); 0.5–1.6 s the rock path draws in under the ring and "32,000 KM" ticks in; hold to 3.2 s; 3.2–3.6 s fade out. Nothing holds still over 4 s. Write the tick times into a sidecar JSON so the assembler can lay the house tick (≤1 per 0.5 s).
- **House rules:** inside the 16:9 centre band of the 9:16 frame (y 656–1264), label lines 11–12% of that band's height (~67–73 px cap height), Arial Black white with dark outline, ≤4 words per label, no black slab or panel (it rides over the moving rock/limb plate), no sourced chart or diagram.
- **Leave:** assembly to the next job. No spend.

jobs.body:
**Packaging panel: 024 Light Speed: title, thumbnails A/B/C (abc_v03) and upload package (airs Sun 1 Nov)** (Ben, 14 Oct 2026: other models critique titles, thumbnails and packaging before the Chief passes them).

You are one of three independent critics. Don't read the other critics' files in `05_Analytics/tests/panels/owb-024-lightspeed/`.

Look at:
- `02_Video-Projects/024_What-Happens-If-You-Travel-Near-Light-Speed/11_Upload-Package/PACKAGE_MANIFEST.json`
- `02_Video-Projects/024_What-Happens-If-You-Travel-Near-Light-Speed/11_Upload-Package/Descriptions`
- `02_Video-Projects/024_What-Happens-If-You-Travel-Near-Light-Speed/08_Thumbnail/abc_v03`
- `02_Video-Projects/024_What-Happens-If-You-Travel-Near-Light-Speed/01_Script`

Score each 1–10 and give **one concrete rewrite** for anything under 8:
1. **Title:** curiosity gap, clarity, would someone type it (search), under about 60 characters, no clickbait we can't pay off.
2. **Thumbnail at phone size** (look at it at 168×94): one subject, a clear emotion or danger, 2–3 words at most, strong contrast,
   readable, and nothing important under the bottom-right duration badge.
3. **Title + thumbnail together:** do they add to each other, or repeat the same words?
4. **First 30 seconds / Short hook** (when a script or cut is given): does it answer or sharpen the promise at once?
5. **Description first line and chapters:** do they work for search without spoiling the payoff?
Then: **"Which would you click, and why?"** (one line) and **"The single change that would most raise CTR."**
Be blunt and specific; no praise padding. Don't change any files except your own critique.

Write your critique to `05_Analytics/tests/panels/owb-024-lightspeed/codex.md` (start it with the date and your name), commit only that file to main from a clean worktree, and mark this job done with your one-line 'single change'. No spend, no YouTube changes.

jobs.title: 032 Titan: fix FLAG rows 1/9/15 + PARTIALs in SOURCES.md and script v01 (Chief notes on J0296)
jobs.body:
Chief review of J0296 (15 Oct 2026 ~17:30 London). Neighbour pass PASS (11 at about 1M+, b15b1529). Facts quote pass: FIX the three FLAG rows before any VO. Source of truth: 02_Video-Projects/032_What-Would-Happen-If-You-Landed-On-Titan/01_Script/SOURCES.md (commit 97a11fdd) and titan_landing_script_master_v00.md. No VO, no picture mint, no Studio change, no spend, no deletes.

Row 1 (surface pressure). Re-point "Where to look" to the pages that actually carry it: Huygens in Nature (https://www.nature.com/articles/nature04314, "the pressure was 1,467 ± 1 hPa") and ESA Facts about Titan ("1500 mbar (1.5 times Earth's)"). Script/VO says "about one and a half times Earth's air pressure". Do not say "50% higher" next to NASA's "60 percent greater"; pick the measured Huygens number. CUT the "5 metres down in a swimming pool" analogy (unsourced, and NASA's own comparison is 15 m in the ocean, which conflicts). SOFTEN "you would not need a pressurised suit" to "the pressure itself wouldn't hurt you; the deadly part is the cold and no oxygen" unless an open NASA/ESA page states the no-pressure-suit point, in which case quote it.

Row 9 (air mix, gravity, density). Re-point to NASA Science Titan Facts ("mostly nitrogen (about 95 percent) and methane (about 5 percent), with small amounts of other carbon-rich compounds") and Dragonfly Why-Titan ("four times denser than Earth's and its gravity is about 1/7th of Earth's"). Script keeps "about 95% nitrogen, about 5% methane", "about four times denser", "about one-seventh of Earth's gravity". CUT "hydrogen cyanide" by name (say "traces of other carbon-rich gases"), and CUT the 0.138 g and 5.3 vs 1.225 kg/m3 figures from VO and charts unless a named open page quotes them verbatim.

Row 15 (flight). The 28x lift-to-weight is our own arithmetic, so keep it only as a labelled on-screen sum ("4x the air, 1/7 the weight, roughly 28x easier to stay up"), not as a quoted or attributed fact. The human flapping-wing flight claim needs an open source with a verbatim quote (e.g. a NASA/ESA/APL page or open Lorenz text); if none is found, SOFTEN to "flying is so easy there that NASA is sending a flying drone, Dragonfly" (quote https://dragonfly.jhuapl.edu/What-Is-Dragonfly/ "make flying an ideal way to travel"). Do not attribute a calculation to Lorenz without an open link.

Done when: the three rows are re-anchored with verbatim quotes and URLs and marked OK (or the claim is cut/softened in both SOURCES.md and the script), the 13 PARTIAL rows are each either re-anchored to the page that carries them or softened, the script master is bumped to v01 with a short change note, and both are committed. Then park for Chief with the commit hash. No VO until Chief PASSes.

jobs.title: HOS 013 Darwin–Wallace: script v02 (Chief FIX on J0299 v01: 4 chronology fixes + Wallace age)
jobs.body:
FIX v02 of HOS 013 Darwin–Wallace script master (Chief review of J0299 v01 at HOS 9db5a26, 15 Oct ~18:00 London). v01 is strong (review:script 92.6, 1,235 words, teach plan and Part 01 timings kept, risky numbers correctly softened). It is FIX, not PASS, only for four spoken chronology slips and one age word. Change only these lines; keep everything else in v01 as is.

File: 02_Video-Projects/013_Darwin-Wallace-Evolution/01_Script/darwin_script_master_v02.md (copy v01, then edit). Update FACT_NOTES to v02 with the new rows.

1. Part 03, 1844 order. The sealed essay and the letter to Emma (5 July 1844) came BEFORE *Vestiges* (published October 1844). v01's "In 1844, an unsigned book ... torn apart ... So that year he wrote out his theory" implies the book caused the essay. Reorder so the essay comes first, then the book: e.g. "In 1844 he wrote it all out, about 230 pages, sealed it, and left Emma a letter ... A few months later, an unsigned book claiming life had changed over time was torn apart by scientists." Keep "like confessing a murder" (Hooker, 11 Jan 1844) and the Emma line.
2. Part 04, grief order. Darwin's "rather lose the credit than seem unfair" letter to Lyell is 25 June 1858; Charles Waring Darwin died 28 June. v01's "that same month, his baby son died ... In grief, Darwin said he would rather lose the credit" reverses them. Put the fairness line first, then the death ("Three days later, his baby son died of scarlet fever."). Part 05's "grieving for his son" on 1 July stays (correct).
3. Part 05, "neither had been asked how it should be done" is wrong for Darwin: he put the matter in Lyell's and Hooker's hands. Say Wallace was never asked (e.g. "Wallace hadn't even been asked. He was still in the islands, and didn't know for months.").
4. Part 05, first printing. The ~1,250 copies were all taken by booksellers at Murray's trade sale on 22 Nov 1859, two days before the 24 Nov publication date. Replace "took the whole first printing on the first day" with the stronger true fact: booksellers had ordered every copy before it even went on sale. Fix the 6:25 VISUAL MUST to match (DATA: about 1,250 copies, sold out before publication day; SCALE line likewise).
5. Wallace was 35 in June 1858 (born 8 Jan 1823). Drop "young" for Wallace in Part 01 VO ("a letter arrived from a collector on the other side of the world") and in the 0:52 VISUAL (a man in his mid-thirties). "Young man who didn't even label his birds" stays (that is Darwin, 26 in 1835).

Soft (no change needed): 11 WHO cards instead of v00's 14 is accepted, since the cut people aren't spoken; don't add names to reach 14.

Keep 1,200–1,300 spoken words, Part 01 cold, both after-act tags. Re-run review:script (must stay >= 90). Spend nothing: no TTS, no picture, no paid API, no Studio change. Commit to HOS main, then `python3 scripts/jobs.py done <id> --agent <you> --result "013 script v02 at <sha>, review:script <score>, <words> words" --ref <sha> --git`. ### Must fix (spoken numbers / unsupported specifics)
1. **Row 10 (SAA altitudes).** Drop `from ~1,000 km`. Named NASA page says the innermost belt begins about 400 miles (~640 km), not ~1,000 km. Keep reverse-flux / SAA weak-spot language that is quoted. For the dip altitude, either quote Wikipedia SAA `200 kilometres` with that URL in Where-to-look, or soften to "closer to Earth than usual" without a km figure. Keep the ISS ~400 km comparison only if a named page states ISS orbit height; else cut that half-sentence.
2. **Row 11 (Hubble / ISS / Hitomi).** Soften Hubble cadence to STScI's "seven to nine orbits in a row" (or "several times a day"), not "up to ~10 times a day". Do not say Hitomi was destroyed by the SAA — JAXA's official report does not attribute the 2016 anomaly to the SAA; cut Hitomi or hedge to "some satellites have glitched after SAA passes" with a page that actually says so. ISS: exterior instruments are on the NASA Goddard page; do not say "ISS laptops" unless you keep the Shuttle-laptop Wikipedia line and label it as such.
3. **Row 15 (backup multipoles %).** Change `10–20%` to about `10%` (BGS reversals.html). Drop `20%` — not on opened pages. Keep "never vanishes / multipoles remain".
4. **Row 18 (4, 6, or 8 poles).** Drop the specific `4, 6, or 8`. Use "multiple magnetic poles" / Glatzmaier language (Africa / Tahiti examples OK). Keep 1,000–10,000 year transition and the generations comparison as our own labelled arithmetic if kept.

### Soft hedges (drop or rephrase; keep the rest of the claim)
5. **Row 3:** drop the month `August` (keep 1905 / published 1906 / Brunhes / Pontfarein / reverse magnetisation).
6. **Row 4:** keep 1929 / Matuyama / Japan and Manchuria from the 1929 paper; put life years and `about 780,000 years` only where Wikipedia/NASA support them (or move the age to the Brunhes–Matuyama line already OK in row 5).
7. **Row 6:** say `about 3,000 km` (not `~2,890 km`); `iron-rich` liquid outer core (drop `and-nickel` unless quoted); `temperatures similar to the surface of the Sun` (not `hotter than`). Re-point Where-to-look off the 404 BGS URL onto `geomag.bgs.ac.uk/education/reversals.html` / ESA / NASA.
8. **Row 9:** say South America / South Atlantic (ESA/NASA wording), not `Brazil`, unless a named page says Brazil.
9. **Row 1:** re-point Where-to-look to NOAA wandering poles + ESA Swarm + NASA Flip-Flop (the numbers live there). Keep marathon comparison only as labelled our-own arithmetic. Named BGS overview URL is 404 — do not cite it.
10. **Row 16:** either keep `~1,000 g/cm²` with the NASA Langley PDF and say the 10 m water line is our unit conversion, or switch the spoken analogy to BGS's "concrete layer some 13 feet thick". Do not imply a page says "10 metres of water" unless it does.

OK rows 2, 5, 7, 8, 12, 13, 14, 17, 19: leave spoken claims as is; you may still refresh Exact-quote cells if cleaner.

jobs.title: Daily Studio read: long films (impressions, CTR, views, avg % viewed) + Shorts (views, avg % viewed, stayed to watch) -> tracker
jobs.body: Free, read-only. Runs daily after the 06:40 snapshot and must finish before 09:00 London (Ben, 12 Oct 22:19). 1) In YouTube Studio, read only, change nothing: Orbit With Ben in the Orbit Studio browser (CDP 9223); History of Science in its own signed-in Studio session (never the 9222 Flow browser for Orbit pages). 2) For every long film (format long in 05_Analytics/dashboard/data.json, both channels), open Analytics > Reach for the video, period Lifetime, and read Impressions and Impressions click-through rate (%), and on Overview/Engagement the lifetime Views, Average view duration (seconds) and Average percentage viewed (%; if Studio shows only duration, compute duration / video length x 100). 2b) For every Short (both channels), read lifetime Views, Average percentage viewed (%) and 'Stayed to watch' (%, Studio's Shorts engagement figure, viewed vs swiped away); write them under the same videos map as "views", "avgViewPct" and "stayedToWatch" (Ben, 12 Oct 22:50). 3) Write 05_Analytics/<owb|hos>/studio_ctr.json: {"readAt": <ISO UTC>, "period": "lifetime", "videos": {"<videoId>": {"impressions": <int>, "impressionsCtr": <number, % e.g. 3.8>, "views": <int>, "avgViewSeconds": <int>, "avgViewPct": <number, %>}}}. A film Studio can't show yet: leave it out. 4) Rebuild: cd 07_Content-Ops && npx tsx scripts/analytics-report.ts (it merges studio_ctr.json into data.json; Studio values take priority on the tracker), then python3 scripts/board_publish.py so /tracker's 'Long films vs targets' panel fills in. 5) Commit only those files to main with a message naming the counts, then jobs.py done <id> --result "<n> OWB + <m> HOS longs; CTR hits vs 4%: ..." --git. Never: edit any video, title, thumbnail or setting; spend anything; paid API.

Runs daily after the 06:40 snapshot and must finish before 09:00 London (Ben, 12 Oct 22:19). 1) In YouTube Studio, read only, change nothing: Orbit With Ben in the Orbit Studio browser (CDP 9223); History of Science in its own signed-in Studio session (never the 9222 Flow browser for Orbit pages). 2) For every long film (format long in 05_Analytics/dashboard/data.json, both channels), open Analytics > Reach for the video, period Lifetime, and read Impressions and Impressions click-through rate (%), and on Overview/Engagement the lifetime Views, Average view duration (seconds) and Average percentage viewed (%; if Studio shows only duration, compute duration / video length x 100). 2b) For every Short (both channels), read lifetime Views, Average percentage viewed (%) and 'Stayed to watch' (%, Studio's Shorts engagement figure, viewed vs swiped away); write them under the same videos map as "views", "avgViewPct" and "stayedToWatch" (Ben, 12 Oct 22:50). 3) Write 05_Analytics/<owb|hos>/studio_ctr.json: {"readAt": <ISO UTC>, "period": "lifetime", "videos": {"<videoId>": {"impressions": <int>, "impressionsCtr": <number, % e.g. 3.8>, "views": <int>, "avgViewSeconds": <int>, "avgViewPct": <number, %>}}}. A film Studio can't show yet: leave it out. 4) Rebuild: cd 07_Content-Ops && npx tsx scripts/analytics-report.ts (it merges studio_ctr.json into data.json; Studio values take priority on the tracker), then python3 scripts/board_publish.py so /tracker's 'Long films vs targets' panel fills in. 5) Commit only those files to main with a message naming the counts, then jobs.py done <id> --result "<n> OWB + <m> HOS longs; CTR hits vs 4%: ..." --git. Never: edit any video, title, thumbnail or setting; spend anything; paid API.

jobs.title: URGENT Mini disk: move old render scratch + ready films to the NAS (sha256-verified) to free 20 GB+ for 024 v06 (J0792)
jobs.body:
**Ben, 21 Oct 2026 (in chat with Claude): "can we use the nas to help free space now".** That is Ben's approval for this job, including removing the local copy of each file **after** its NAS copy is sha256-verified (AGENTS.md "Render scratch" and "YouTube staging folder" rules). It is not approval to delete anything on the NAS, any master that exists only on the Mini, or anything git-tracked.

Why now: the Mini has ~8.5 GiB free, under the 20 GB render floor. J0792 (024 v06, airs Sun 1 Nov, Private upload by Thu 29 Oct) cannot start until there is room.

Do, in order, and stop at the first step that fails:

1. **Is the NAS really usable?** `/Volumes/data` must be mounted (check `mount | grep /Volumes/data`, never write into an unmounted path: it lands on the Mini disk). Time a listing and a write: `timeout 20 ls /Volumes/data/mac-mini-archive/` and `timeout 20 sh -c 'echo ok > /Volumes/data/mac-mini-archive/.probe && cat /Volumes/data/mac-mini-archive/.probe && rm /Volumes/data/mac-mini-archive/.probe'`. If either hangs or fails: post one line on #99 ("NAS hung: listing/write timed out; Ben to restart the NAS or remount /Volumes/data on the Mini"), block this job `needs Ben: NAS hung`, stop.
2. **The stalled J0775 copy.** Read `~/_desk/logs/J0775-scratch.log` and check for `J0775-scratch.done`. If tmux `codex-j0775-scratch` is still running with an empty log, kill it (nothing local was removed yet). Never start a second copy alongside a running one.
3. **Measure first.** `du -sh` each candidate and post the list (path, size, film, version) on #99 before moving anything:
   - render scratch under /private/tmp older than each film's current and previous version (keep those two);
   - finished films already in OWB UAT / HOS UAT that are scheduled or waiting to go out → `mac-mini-archive/youtube-staging/<film-id>/`, per the staging rule (the upload then reads from the NAS path).
4. **Move, biggest first, one folder at a time:** write to a fresh dated folder (`mac-mini-archive/mini-tmp-scratch/2026-10-21/<film>/…`); `rsync -a`; make a sha256 manifest on both sides; compare; only on an exact match remove that folder's local copy and leave `MOVED_TO_NAS.txt` (NAS path + manifest path). A mismatch or a timeout: keep the local copy, note it, go on to the next folder.
5. Stop when the Mini has ≥ 25 GB free, or the candidates run out. Post on #99: GB freed, free space now, what moved where, anything kept and why. Mark this job done; then J0792 can claim.

Run long copies detached (tmux) with a `.done` file, as J0775 did, so the job survives the wake cap. £0 spend; no Studio or YouTube changes.

jobs.title: refill.py: never add a backlog copy while one of that key is open, claimed or blocked (fix the ~28-copies-per-family flood)
jobs.body:
Bug (Chief sweep, 21 Oct 2026). Between 16 and 21 Oct `scripts/refill.py refill` added 28-30 copies of each of 15 backlog keys (406 jobs); Chief cancelled 395 of them today (jobs commit e09ab18a4). Cause in `do_refill.busy()`: a key only counted as busy while a job was `open` or `claimed`. Every worker parked its copy (`blocked`, 'parked for Chief: ...') within minutes, which freed the key, and after `every_h` (8-48 h, and the 'never empty' fallback ignores even that) the next copy was added. Copies blocked for other reasons (e.g. 'Storage prerequisite: 7.8 GiB free', J0791/J0797/J0798) never counted at all. Claude's #246 (1fb349fb1, 21 Oct 16:24) capped this at PARK_CAP = 2 parked copies and paused 8 keys; that limits the flood but still allows a second copy while one waits for Chief, and still ignores non-'parked' blocked copies.

Fix (code only, on a branch + PR, do not hand-edit queue.json):
1. `busy(key)` is true while ANY job of that key is `open`, `claimed` or `blocked` (whatever the block reason), i.e. `LIVE` already defined in the file. Drop PARK_CAP (or set it to 1 and make it moot). The 'never empty' fallback must use the same `busy()`.
2. A done/cancelled copy frees the key; `every_h` still applies after it.
3. `escalate` unchanged, but post at most one escalation line per key per 24 h (it re-posted the same items for five days).
4. Tests in `scripts/test_refill.py`: (a) key with one open copy -> no add; (b) claimed -> no add; (c) blocked 'parked for Chief' -> no add; (d) blocked 'Storage prerequisite...' (no 'parked' text) -> no add; (e) only done/cancelled copies and every_h elapsed -> one add; (f) the never-empty fallback with every key busy -> adds nothing; (g) daily_at item (studio-ctr-daily) with yesterday's copy still blocked -> no add. Run the whole test file plus `python3 scripts/refill.py refill --min 3` against a copy of today's queue.json and show it adds 0 copies of any key that has a live copy.

Success: refill never adds a copy of a key while one is open, claimed, or blocked/parked for Chief; tests green in CI; PR parked for Chief merge. £0, no queue edits beyond the job's own jobs.py calls.

jobs.title: GitHub: delete 110 merged branches + archive-tag and delete 13 finished ones (Ben's go 21 Oct)
jobs.body:
**Ben, 21 Oct 2026 (in chat with Claude): "go branches".** Delete the 108 GitHub branches of orbit-with-ben whose work is already in main. The list with each branch's tip sha is `jobs/data/branch_cleanup_2026-10-21.txt` (Claude checked every one: merged into main, or its merged PR's head is the branch tip). The cloud session can't delete branches (the proxy refuses), so the Mini does it with its own GitHub login.

1. `git pull` main, `git fetch --prune origin`.
2. For each `branch sha` line (skip the `#` line): only if `git rev-parse origin/<branch>` still equals that sha, `git push origin --delete <branch>`. A different sha (someone pushed since) or a missing branch: skip it and note it. Never delete `main`, `mini-heartbeat`, `claude-heartbeat`, `board-data`, or any branch not in the file.
3. `git fetch --prune origin`; post on #99: deleted N, skipped (name + why), branches left. Mark this job done.

4. **Archive, then delete** (Ben, 21 Oct: "yes clean up"): for each `branch sha` line in `jobs/data/branch_archive_2026-10-21.txt`, only if `origin/<branch>` still equals that sha: `git tag archive/<branch> <sha>`, `git push origin archive/<branch>`, check `git ls-remote origin refs/tags/archive/<branch>` returns the sha, and only then `git push origin --delete <branch>`. Nothing is lost: the tag keeps every commit.
5. Keep the three `backup/...` branches as they are.

Nothing else: no PR closes, no other branches. £0.

jobs.title: Board: sync film stages from done jobs so 'Since yesterday' shows real progress
jobs.body:
Ben, 21 Oct 2026 (Kanban screenshot): "Since yesterday does not seem to be showing progress". It showed 0 videos advanced with 26 jobs finished. Cause: the board's percentages come from each film's `02_Video-Projects/<film>/status.json` stages, and those only move when a job carries `film` + `stage` or someone runs `studio.py`. Most jobs (and every Chief PASS) don't, so stages sat in `review`/`doing` for days (021 still said edit=review, upload=doing 10 days after it went live; Claude fixed 021, 025, 030 by hand on 21 Oct).

Fix (code, PR, tests):
1. `scripts/stage_sync.py`: for each OWB film, find stages in `review`/`doing`/`blocked` whose job(s) are done with a Chief PASS/KEEP result (match by film id in title or `film`, stage by `stage` field or the job's `kind` via scripts/routing.py KINDS), and propose `done` (with the job id as ref). Upload receipts (`11_Upload-Package/*UPLOAD_RESULT*.json`) set upload done with the `ref <id> (Private, publishAt …)` note the board reads. Dry-run by default; `--apply --git` writes through `studio.py` and pushes.
2. Run it from the hourly studio run (Chief's step 5) with `--apply`, and report what moved in one #99 line.
3. Tests: a PASS-done picture job moves picture review→done; a FIX result does not; a job without a film is ignored; an upload receipt sets the scheduled note.
4. In `jobs.py add`, warn when a job names a film (`\b0\d\d\b` with OWB/HOS) but has no `--film/--stage`.

jobs.body:
**023 Venus Short `venus_95pct_wide` v02: Chief FIX on J0824's v01.** Chief reviewed v01 (24.5 s, 55 words, all gates PASS) on 22 Oct (#99). Keep everything that works: frame-0 '95% / AS WIDE' hook on the cloudy Venus globe with the 16% push, the v05e VO lift 46.90-69.12 s (opens on a complete thought, stands alone), captions, FOUR-FIFTHS MASS bar 4.3-6.85 s, title card 'What Happened / to Venus?' 9-14 s, end card with VBaYRPp85Sw, house SFX, cover. The 0:21 SDO transit soft-sun WARN is accepted (real NASA footage under 'closer to the sun').

Fix (both found by Chief in the v01 master, not on the sheets):
1. **Leaked long-film label + dissolve at 15.87-16.00 s** (cut s04_full_globe -> s05_ridged_highlands): the long's baked lower-third 'Alpha Regio / Venus's oldest r...' and its cross-dissolve show for ~4 frames at the start of s05 (v05e offset 338.55 s), and the last frames of s04 (v05e 221.20 s + 2.9 s) already carry the incoming dissolve ghost. Move s05's in-point later until every frame is clean (try ~338.80 s) and end s04 before the long's dissolve starts (shift its v05e offset earlier, same 2.9 s length). Keep the row timeline in/outs. Check every frame of every cut +/-0.2 s at full frame rate: no long-film labels, no ghosts.
2. **One-frame double caption at caption boundaries** (e.g. 2.00 s shows 'VENUS IS NINETY-FIVE' on top of 'PERCENT AS WIDE'): the assembler's `overlay ... enable='between(t,s,e)'` is inclusive at both ends, so a frame landing exactly on a boundary shows both captions. Use `enable='gte(t,s)*lt(t,e)'` for the captions (and the hook/title/card overlays). The same pattern is in the other 023 lift assemblers (lift_90x_air shows it at ~0.70 s): fix it here and note it on #99 for a backlog fix; don't rebuild the others in this job.

Render `venus_95pct_wide_v02.mp4` in the same 06_Final-Exports, rerun gate_shorts_open, sfx_kit, polish_gate and picture_qa, make new contact + open sheets plus a full-frame-rate strip of every cut +/-0.2 s. Commit the builder and sidecars (not the mp4; *.mp4 is gitignored). v01's sidecars and builder are still untracked, so commit those too. Post the cut, sheets, cut strip and gate output on #99, then block 'parked for Chief: Short PASS'. Never upload. Spend nothing.

jobs.title: Daily Studio read: long films (impressions, CTR, views, avg % viewed) + Shorts (views, avg % viewed, stayed to watch) -> tracker
jobs.body: Free, read-only. Runs daily after the 06:40 snapshot and must finish before 09:00 London (Ben, 12 Oct 22:19). 1) In YouTube Studio, read only, change nothing: Orbit With Ben in the Orbit Studio browser (CDP 9223); History of Science in its own signed-in Studio session (never the 9222 Flow browser for Orbit pages). 2) For every long film (format long in 05_Analytics/dashboard/data.json, both channels), open Analytics > Reach for the video, period Lifetime, and read Impressions and Impressions click-through rate (%), and on Overview/Engagement the lifetime Views, Average view duration (seconds) and Average percentage viewed (%; if Studio shows only duration, compute duration / video length x 100). 2b) For every Short (both channels), read lifetime Views, Average percentage viewed (%) and 'Stayed to watch' (%, Studio's Shorts engagement figure, viewed vs swiped away); write them under the same videos map as "views", "avgViewPct" and "stayedToWatch" (Ben, 12 Oct 22:50). 3) Write 05_Analytics/<owb|hos>/studio_ctr.json: {"readAt": <ISO UTC>, "period": "lifetime", "videos": {"<videoId>": {"impressions": <int>, "impressionsCtr": <number, % e.g. 3.8>, "views": <int>, "avgViewSeconds": <int>, "avgViewPct": <number, %>}}}. A film Studio can't show yet: leave it out. 4) Rebuild: cd 07_Content-Ops && npx tsx scripts/analytics-report.ts (it merges studio_ctr.json into data.json; Studio values take priority on the tracker), then python3 scripts/board_publish.py so /tracker's 'Long films vs targets' panel fills in. 5) Commit only those files to main with a message naming the counts, then jobs.py done <id> --result "<n> OWB + <m> HOS longs; CTR hits vs 4%: ..." --git. Never: edit any video, title, thumbnail or setting; spend anything; paid API.

Compare with last week. Post a summary on desk #180. 4b) Shorts lab (Ben, 21 Oct 2026, from Gemini's read of the HOS gold Short: 44% viewed on 25 s, the feed stopped after the first pool): for every Short public 48 h or more and not yet in the table, add one row to the Shorts lab table in 05_Analytics/LEARNINGS.md: id, title, length (s), views, stayed-to-watch % (Studio's Viewed vs swiped away; from the daily Studio read, studio_ctr.json), average % viewed, the second where the retention curve (Analytics API audienceWatchRatio by elapsedVideoTimeRatio) falls most, and what is on screen and said at that second (from the Short's cut list and VO words). Targets: stayed-to-watch 70%+, average viewed 70%+ (100%+ means rewatches). 4c) Learnings: turn this week's evidence into at most 3 rules or tests in the Learnings table of LEARNINGS.md (rule, evidence with ids and numbers, status: test/proven/dropped). jobs.body:
60% stayed-to-watch re-cuts, batch 1 (Chief, 24 Oct 2026; Ben's target is 60%+ stayed-to-watch on every Short). This is a local v02 render only.

Why: standalone S1 Mercury vlkj8RQKmH8 aired 24 Oct at 32.1% stayed (Studio). Its opening is the template every standalone Short shares: a grey NASA still with a slow push (PIA11351 1.00→1.04 over 5.5 s, top ~45% black), the setting said first ("On Mercury, [0.33 s pause] one day lasts two years", so the payoff words land at ~2.0 s), a meta-promise at ~2.2–3.2 s ("Stay, and I'll show you how"), a first cut at 5.5 s and a 3.0 s tail after the last word. The best Short with 100+ views, y-SPHQ0-VjQ (56.0%), opens on full-frame moving SDO video. Rules: .cursor/rules/orbit-build-shorts.mdc → "60% stayed-to-watch" (PR #266).

Shorts in this batch, by air date:
- S2 Neptune oyRcrFTYyDY (Tue 27 Oct 11:30 London). Must be ready by Mon 26 Oct 12:00 London so Ben can decide on a swap.
- S3 ISS sunrises XKlq0TK1OVA (Sat 31 Oct 11:30 London).

Files: 00_Brand/Channel-Setup/audits/STANDALONE_SHORTS_TEST_2026-10/ (SCRIPTS_v01.md, 06_Final-Exports/owb_sa_s{2,3}_*_v01_meta.json, _assemble_standalone_shorts_v01.py, vo_v01/trim/).

For each Short:
1) VO, spending £0 (no new TTS). Cut the "Stay, and I'll show you…" sentence out of the existing trimmed VO with ffmpeg. Close the gap to a breath of 0.15 s or less. Keep the first spoken word at 0.15 s or earlier.
2) Frame 0 must be moving payoff footage, full-bleed. Use public-domain NASA/JPL/SVS motion that is free to download (e.g. Voyager 2 Neptune approach or cloud-band animation; ISS Earth-terminator timelapse from the ISS crew-earth-observations video library), or a clip already on disk. Only if no motion exists at all: a fast move (≥15% scale or a clear pan inside 1.0 s) plus a visible event by 0.5 s. A still pushed ≤1.10 fails. The subject fills ≥60% of the frame.
3) First cut by 3.0 s, every later plate held 4 s at most. Hook caption on frame 0 as now. Gap from last word to loop point 1.5 s or less. Matched loop cut back to the frame-0 picture (crossfade 0.3 s at most).
4) Render owb_sa_s{2,3}_*_v02.mp4 next to v01. v01 stays untouched. Write a v02 meta.json with the six brief fields (frame-0 source and zoom, first-word onset, surprise-word time, first cut, last word→loop, meta-promise n). Make a frames sheet. Run gate_shorts_open.py check --air-date, polish_gate, music_gate and sfx_kit level. All must PASS.

Hard rules: £0 (no paid API, TTS or picture generation), no upload, no Studio change, no Public, no Replace, no deletions, no force-push. Commit only the v02 meta, gate text and frames sheet (media stays out of git, as now).

End with: jobs.py block <id> --reason "parked for Chief: S2/S3 v02 PASS; Ben to OK swap (new Private upload on the same slot, v01 kept private and unscheduled, nothing deleted)" --git

jobs.title: Weekly OWB audit: our YouTube numbers + competitors -> next-video improvements
jobs.body: Weekly growth audit for Orbit With Ben (aim: numbers up month on month). 1) Pull last 28 days and last 7 days from YouTube Analytics with the read-only tracker sign-in (YT_ANALYTICS_REFRESH_TOKEN_OWB; 05_Analytics tools): views, impressions CTR, AVD/retention curves, subs per video, Shorts vs longs, traffic sources, search terms. 2) What's working and what isn't: top/bottom 3 by CTR and retention, with the frame or title that explains it. 3) Competitors: 5 reference channels (Astrum, History of the Universe, SEA, Kurzgesagt, melodysheep) last 30 days via public pages/yt-dlp metadata only: titles, thumbs, lengths, view velocity, topics trending. 4) Write 05_Analytics/weekly_audit/OWB_<YYYY-MM-DD>.md: findings, then 3-5 concrete changes for the next films in production (title/thumb/opening/length/topic), each tied to a film id, plus 3 new video ideas ranked by evidence. Compare with last week's file and say what moved. 4b) Shorts lab (Ben, 21 Oct 2026, from Gemini's read of the HOS gold Short: 44% viewed on 25 s, the feed stopped after the first pool): for every Short public 48 h or more and not yet in the table, add one row to the Shorts lab table in 05_Analytics/LEARNINGS.md: id, title, length (s), views, stayed-to-watch % (Studio's Viewed vs swiped away; from the daily Studio read, studio_ctr.json), average % viewed, the second where the retention curve (Analytics API audienceWatchRatio by elapsedVideoTimeRatio) falls most, and what is on screen and said at that second (from the Short's cut list and VO words). Targets: stayed-to-watch 60%+ (Ben's floor, 24 Oct; 70%+ stretch), average viewed 70%+ (Ben's second floor, 24 Oct 20:03; aim 100%+ = rewatches via loop endings). 4d) Two-target check (Ben, 24 Oct 2026; orbit-build-shorts.mdc → '60% stayed-to-watch' and '70% average viewed'): also grade average viewed LOOP ≥100 / PASS ≥70 / WATCH 50–69.9 / MISS <50 with runtime, longest plate hold, payoff time and whether the last line loops into line 1; for every Short with a 48 h+ Studio read in the last 14 days, list stayed-to-watch % against the 60% target as PASS (≥60), WATCH (45–59.9), MISS (<45) or too few (<100 Studio views), plus the frame-0 source (video, or a still and its zoom), the first-word onset, the first cut (s) and whether a meta-promise is present. Say which of the six 60% rules the misses break, and propose re-cuts only for Shorts not yet public (local renders only; any swap goes to Ben). 4c) Learnings: turn this week's evidence into at most 3 rules or tests in the Learnings table of LEARNINGS.md (rule, evidence with ids and numbers, status: test/proven/dropped). A rule proven on 3+ Shorts is proposed to the Chief for the Shorts brief and the playbook; a test names the next 2-4 Shorts it runs on. Keep the audit itself to one page: what moved, the lab rows, the rules. Spend nothing: existing subscriptions and free tools only, no paid API, no TTS or picture generation in these growth jobs (credits are for pipeline VO and picture; floors are 0, Ben 12 Oct 14:46), no Studio or publish change. End with jobs.py block <id> --reason "parked for Chief: <what to decide>" --git.

dM1OgGPAYvw "What If Earth Stopped Spinning?" (027 lift_sudden_air, airs Mon 26 Oct 11:30 London). MUST be parked by Sun 25 Oct 20:00 London. If late, v01 airs as scheduled.

Fix = STAYED60_UPCOMING_AUDIT_2026-10-25.md #1:
1. Trim "Now imagine the impossible." (0.00–1.80 s) from _work_v02/stem_vo.wav so "Earth's" starts ≤0.15 s and "stops turning" lands by 1.74 s. Tighten the 4.38→4.98 s and 6.12→6.96 s pauses to ≤0.18 s. If the Short drops under 18 s, add the next sentence from the 027 master VO (44.66–49.50 s) at matched level/room tone.
2. Keep epic_earth_rotation.mp4 at frame 0 (moving, 3.1% black).
3. First cut ≤2.5 s. Split s04 (5.80 s) into two ≤3.5 s moving spans (027 code_out_v06/row10/air.mp4 + Gerst_Earth_timelapses_2017.webm).
4. Remove the 4.0 s end card; matched 1.0 s loop back to the frame-0 EPIC framing.

Same rules for every re-cut (J0916 ruling OWB #264 6389353471, J0918 strict ship gate 6392833473, J0914/J0929 loop rule):
- Local v02 next to v01 in the Short's own 10_Shorts/<slug>/ folder; v01 stays untouched.
- £0: VO trims, reorders and splices from words already recorded on disk only (the Short's own VO stem or the film's locked long VO). No new TTS, Veo, Flow, Omni, Vertex or paid API. If a fix needs words that are not on disk, trim instead.
- Frame 0 is moving, full-bleed footage, ≤30% black, ≥60% subject, no Orbit at frame 0. Subject named and surprise claim spoken by 1.5 s; first word by 0.15 s.
- First cut by 3.0 s (strict gate (b), no moving-shot waiver). Later plates 4.0 s max. No still-to-still cuts.
- No meta-promise ("Stay, and I'll show you…"), no agenda question, no spoken "The full film…" CTA, no end card. The long's title + ID go in the description / Related link, not the picture.
- Payoff number lands at ≥70% of runtime; never answer the title question under the 9–14 s banner.

[Acting Chief Codex, 26 Oct 2026] FIX: the submitted six-cut blanket PASS is rejected. Follow jobs/reviews/J0935/RULING_2026-10-26_CODEX.md (committed on main) before the earlier brief. Levels, PHONE and manifest copies verified; remaining failures: mon09 2.126s surprise; mon09/fri13 below current 22s floor; wed11 answer under banner; missing master-derived transcripts on all six; incomplete 2fps sheets mon09/thu12; picture/words mismatch on rover deck shots; reconcile current Keeper first line with recorded material and c61 without inventing a PASS. Same six air-date steps, local/no-spend only. Do not create swap jobs or Ready for OK cards. Target 1 Nov 20:00 London; no external wait. Assembly primary Cursor Grok 4.7 via existing chain. Earlier/scheduled versions remain untouched.

[Chief] Grok Chief ruling c61 (Mon 26 Oct 07:00 London, OWB #264 6410141575) on **J0935, OWB 60% re-cut batch B** (audit `STAYED60_UPCOMING_AUDIT_2026-10-25.md` #6-#11, J0916 ruling 6389353471). Cursor parked it at 06:38 London (`b70196d9a`, `37d0ef0cd`, `460d5d716`, `3e2de9c0d`, `b36431748`, `c05cd84f0`, all on origin/main).

**Verdict: all six are FIX. No swap jobs and no Ready for OK cards yet.** Most of the audit work is done: the CTAs, agenda questions and end cards are gone, and each claim now lands by 1.5 s on moving footage. But every Short fails the level and _PHONE gates, and five of the six have a broken VO sentence a viewer would hear. Nothing airs differently, because the scheduled versions stay scheduled (v01, or v02 for wed11/fri13). J0935 is reopened so the mini can build the next version of each. Nothing needed from Ben.

**Batch-wide (all six)**
- **Level ✗ on all 6.** ebur128 peak=true on the AAC gives I / TP: mon09 **-14.7 / -1.5**, wed11 -14.5 / **-1.4**, thu12 **-14.9 / -1.5**, fri13 **-14.9 / -1.5**, mon16 **-15.1 / -1.5**, wed18 -14.3 / **-1.4**. loudnorm gives -15.08/-1.49, -14.75/-1.36, -15.01/-1.49, -15.10/-1.49, -15.29/-1.46, -14.42/-1.41. Target is -14.0 ±0.5 LUFS with TP ≤ -1.6 dBTP. Normalise the final mix to -14.0, limit to -1.6 dBTP (alimiter `latency=1`), and make the gate fail on these numbers. The metas already admit -14.7 / -14.9 / -14.9 / -15.1, the same gap c59 found in batch C.
- **No _PHONE.mp4 ✗.** Only `<stem>_PHONE.jpg` contact tiles exist (repo, OWB UAT, NAS), so the board's Play button would have nothing to open. Build `<stem>_PHONE.mp4` (720×1280, same frames and audio) for each.
- **No sha256_manifest.json ✗.** UAT/NAS carry `MANIFEST.sha256`, and mon09's lists only the master. Write `sha256_manifest.json` covering master + _PHONE.mp4 + sheets + meta in all three places.
- **What's fine ✓.** The masters match across repo, OWB UAT and NAS (`youtube-staging/025|026/<stem>/`) and the meta: mon09 `0ed62579`, wed11 `8ae224ce`, thu12 `2bdcfcd8`, fri13 `f080895c`, mon16 `3b1e2a5f`, wed18 `5af000f0`. All are 1080×1920 @ 30 fps with AAC 48 kHz. The dark-run check is clear: no run ≥ 3 frames with > 85% of pixels below luma 20. OCR on every 3rd frame (tesseract, 720×1280) finds 0 URLs, logos, copyright lines, ids or file names. The only hits are caption words, "June 10" (the date label in NASA's 2018 sky-darkening sequence, a correct date call-out, so I'm accepting it) and hardware-texture misreads. No CTA, agenda question, meta-promise or end card. **v01s untouched ✓:** the six J0935 commits only add files; the v01 metas and assemblers are unchanged; 026 v01 masters on NAS `shorts_j0141/` are mon16 `24a5552b` and wed18 `be7c6121` (22 Oct). wed11 v02 and fri13 v02 (the scheduled files) are untouched. £0, and every plate and VO word was already on disk.

**Per Short**
1. **iyvWYFP_ETA mon09 night cold v02 (Mon 9 Nov) FIX.** (a) **Sentence 1 is broken:** "On Mars, minus 90 degrees. The night can fall…" The reorder dropped "to" and left "the night can fall" hanging (captions read THE NIGHT CAN / FALL BATTERIES HATE). Put the recorded sentence back in its own order, "On Mars, the night can fall to minus 90 degrees", and close the 0.16 s and 0.40 s pauses (audit #6) so "minus 90" lands by 1.5 s. If it still lands late, tighten sentence 1 only, with atempo ≤ 1.08. (b) **At 12.1-13.0 s a stitched mosaic shows up to 60% black edges** under "In 2009" (f/mon09_2009.jpg). It's also Curiosity's deck, but Spirit is the rover in that line. Crop inside the mosaic to full-bleed, or use a MER/Spirit or plain-ground plate. (c) The runtime of 17.6 s is under the 18-24 s band (the gate warned). Fixing (a) and opening the pauses back up to about 0.2 s should bring it to 18-19 s. (d) Level. Fine: moving PIA26673 frame 0 (motion 11.45), first cut 2.53 s, cuts every 3.5 s, "couldn't" at 14.82 s (84%), loop_diff 0.95. Facts check out (about -90 °C nights; Spirit stuck at Troy in 2009, couldn't tilt to the winter Sun).
2. **TtgHNLXfDSs wed11 opening v03 (Wed 11 Nov) FIX.** (a) **The middle is broken:** "Dust should have choked its solar panels within months. It wears them down slowly in ways you already know from home. The cold that kills a phone battery, Martian wind kept sweeping them clean." "It" has no subject, and "The cold that kills a phone battery" is a fragment welded onto the wind line. Drop both long-VO slices ("It wears them down… from home" and "The cold that kills a phone battery"). Join "…within months." straight to "Martian wind kept sweeping them clean." To stay in 23-25 s, add whole sentences that are already on disk, e.g. "The team called them cleaning events. Each one gave the rover back its power, and it kept driving." (as used in thu12), and keep "2018" at ≥ 70%. (b) TP -1.4. Fine: "fourteen years" ends at 1.45 s, Mars at 1.68 s, moving Gale frame 0, first cut 2.53 s, holds ≤ 3.5 s, 2018 at 18.17 s (75%), loop_diff 0.77. Facts check out (90-day mission, about 14.5 years, 2018 global dust storm).
3. **N42gKBbD7tE thu12 length test v02 (Thu 12 Nov) FIX.** (a) **There's a broken sentence:** "Opportunity should have starved within months. Instead, again and again, the team called them cleaning events." The clause that belonged after "again and again" (the wind sweeping the panels) moved to the open, so "Instead, again and again" and "them" now point at nothing. Re-use the same recorded clause there: "Instead, again and again, Martian wind and passing dust devils swept its panels clean. The team called them cleaning events…" That adds about 4 s, which is fine for the 50-60 s test. (b) **33.7-37.1 s is a deck mosaic with black unfilled corners** (up to 41% black) under "last signal / engineers on earth". The 6-8.5 s and 16.5-20 s mosaics also show black corners. Scale or crop inside the mosaic to full-bleed. (c) Level. Fine: "wind" at 0.54 s, moving descent frame 0, first cut 2.5 s, cuts every 3.47 s, no end card, loop_diff 0.66. The story order is kept per the J0916 ruling, so "fourteen" at 17.7 s is accepted. Facts check out (last signal 10 June 2018, more than 1,000 commands over about 8 months).
4. **bSjWiCbB7pY fri13 Ingenuity v03 (Fri 13 Nov) FIX.** (a) **2.5-18.3 s plays as one 16 s hold.** s01-s05 alternate the two Ingenuity flight clips (JPL-20210419 and JPL-20210425) at the same wide framing. My scan finds no visible cut between 2.5 and 18.33 s, and the helicopter is a speck (f/fri13_sheet.jpg). Give each plate a visibly different framing (punch in 2-3x on the craft, a different section of each clip, the PIA24644 shadow) so the picture changes at least every 3.8 s. (b) **The payoff "2024" lands at 13.22 s, which is 69%,** under the ≥ 70% rule (needs ≥ 13.42 s). Add about 0.25 s before "In 2024". (c) Frame 0 motion is 8.67 (< 10, the gate warned). Start the gif where the shadow is already moving. (d) Level. Advisory: the "how" answer (1% air, 2,000 rpm) sits under the 9-14 s banner, so move it out of that window if the re-time allows. Fine: "Mars" at 0.27 s, "seventy-two" at 1.42 s, first cut 2.5 s, 19.17 s, loop to PIA24644 in 1.07 s. Facts check out (built for 5 flights, flew 72, about 1% air density, about 2,400-2,500 rpm, blade damage Jan 2024, still standing).
5. **HZGTovJu_TQ mon16 can't see v02 (Mon 16 Nov) FIX.** (a) **The parallax lines are orphaned:** "Your two eyes are a ruler. Astronomers use the same trick with the whole of Earth's orbit." These were spliced from the long VO without the thumb/wink set-up, so "the same trick" points at nothing. Splice in the long-VO sentence(s) just before "Your two eyes…" that explain the trick, so it's complete. If that pushes it past about 22 s, cut both lines and take the runtime from the paused-out VO. Keep "four years" at ≥ 70%. (b) Level -15.1. (c) Frame 0 motion is 9.25 (< 10, the gate warned), so start the Paranal plate a beat later. Fine: star at 0.48 s, "can't see it" at 1.45 s, first cut 2.53 s, "four years" at 16.87 s (85%), loop_diff 4.32, no end card. Facts check out (Proxima: red dwarf, V ≈ 11, < 1% of the Sun's light, light takes 4.24 yr).
6. **cwU_0WWeNZ4 wed18 Voyager v02 (Wed 18 Nov) FIX.** (a) **The VO is broken and now misleads:** "It is not heading towards Proxima, launched in 1977. After nearly fifty years of flying, moonlight reaches you in just over a second. Sunlight takes about eight minutes. At that speed, the trip would take about 75,000 years." Three long-VO slices are welded mid-sentence, and "At that speed" now follows the sunlight line, so it sounds as if light takes 75,000 years. Rebuild it from whole sentences: "Voyager 1 moves 17 kilometres every second. At that speed, the trip would take about 75,000 years." Then add the light-time ladder (moonlight about 1 s, sunlight 8 min, plus the long VO's whole sentence that Proxima's light takes more than four years) so the distance answer is the payoff at ≥ 70%. End on "And Voyager isn't even heading that way." before the loop. Only use whole recorded sentences. (b) The first cut is at 2.73 s (audit/J0935 ≤ 2.7), and s02-s04 hold 4.0 s each (audit caps s03 at 3.6). Cut at 2.6-2.7 s and keep every plate ≤ 3.6 s. (c) TP -1.4. Fine: "17 kilometres" at 1.0 s, moving Paranal frame 0 (13% black, motion 12.2), no CTA/end card, loop 1.0 s, loop_diff 8.41. Facts check out (17 km/s, launched 1977, about 75,000 yr at that speed, not heading to Proxima).

**What the mini does next (J0935 reopened; build v03, or v04 for wed11/fri13, next to the current files; v01/v02 untouched).** Fix the items above. Re-run gate_shorts_open with --air-date, picture_qa, polish, music and sfx. Then run the **dark-run check**, a **black-edge check** (no run of 15 or more frames with > 30% of pixels below luma 20) and an **OCR pass** on every 3rd frame. Also do a **transcript read-through** (whisper on the master: every sentence must have a subject and verb, with no slice welded mid-clause). Write the measured AAC LUFS/TP and loop_diff into the meta. Commit and push, then copy master + _PHONE.mp4 + sheet + meta + sha256_manifest.json to OWB UAT and NAS. Park as "parked for Chief: <ids> PASS; Ben to OK each swap", each Short by 20:00 London the day before it airs (mon09 Sun 8 Nov). Target the whole batch **by Sun 1 Nov 20:00 London**, ahead of J0936's v03s (air-date order). Any Short that can't pass airs as scheduled. Ben's bars for every Short: ≥ 60% stayed-to-watch and ≥ 70% average viewed, so keep the matched loops.

Same rules for every re-cut (J0916 ruling OWB #264 6389353471, J0918 strict ship gate 6392833473, J0914/J0929 loop rule):

- Frame 0 is moving, full-bleed footage, ≤30% black, ≥60% subject, no Orbit at frame 0. Subject named and surprise claim spoken by 1.5 s; first word by 0.15 s.
