- Payoff number lands at ≥70% of runtime; never answer the title question under the 9–14 s banner.
- Matched loop: last word to loop ≤1.5 s, last frame built from the frame-0 plate at frame-0 framing. Last-vs-frame-0 mean diff ≤15 (text masked); log loop_diff in meta.
- Educational (Ben 11 Oct): keep the existing number/Teach card or code graphic where the v01 has one (inside y=656..1264); don't add new generated assets.
- Keep the v01 title and air slot. Length 18–24 s unless the audit says otherwise.
- Gates: gate_shorts_open --air-date (strict, incl. stayed transcript check), picture_qa, polish_gate, music_gate, sfx level; all PASS. Write the six brief fields, measured LUFS and loop_diff into each v02 meta.
- Commit meta, gate text and 2 fps frame sheets (git add -f). Copy _PHONE + sheets to OWB UAT and NAS.
- No upload, no Studio change, no Public, no Replace, no delete, no force-push. Park as "parked for Chief: <id> v02 PASS; Ben to OK swap". A swap is a new Private upload on the same slot after Chief PASS and Ben's OK, v01 kept private and unscheduled, nothing deleted. If a Short isn't OK'd by 10:30 London on its air day, v01 airs as scheduled; don't slip the slot.

jobs.body:
[Chief] Grok Chief ruling c59 (Mon 26 Oct 05:50 London, OWB #264 6409202315) on **J0936, OWB 60% re-cut v02 batch C** (audit `STAYED60_UPCOMING_AUDIT_2026-10-25.md` #12-#17). Cursor parked it at 05:10 London (`aec9fed53`, `86a0dcd98`, `ae7107641`, `50d6aa308`, `e28eb7d40`, `7309f2f14`, all on origin/main).

**Verdict: all six are FIX. No swap jobs and no Ready for OK cards yet.** The gates passed, but each Short has at least one problem a viewer would notice or that breaks the J0936 rules. The audit fixes are mostly in: the end cards and spoken CTAs are gone, the claim comes first, Gliese 710 is named in sentence 1, and the loops are matched. Nothing airs differently, because all six v01s stay scheduled. J0936 is reopened so the mini carries on with v03s. Nothing needed from Ben.

**Batch-wide (all six)**
- **Level ✗ on 5 of 6.** ebur128 peak=true on the AAC gives I / TP: grapefruit **-15.0 / -1.5**, equator -14.4 / -1.5, comets -14.5 / **-1.4**, wed02 **-15.1 / -1.4**, fri04 **-14.9** / -1.5, night sky **-15.0** / -1.5. loudnorm gives -15.11/-1.49, -14.39/-1.48, -14.71/-1.43, -15.29/-1.42, -15.11/-1.49, -15.29/-1.49. Target is -14.0 ±0.5 LUFS with TP ≤ -1.5 dBTP. Normalise the final mix to -14.0 and limit to -1.6 dBTP with alimiter `latency=1`. The metas already admit -15.0 / -15.1 / -14.8 / -15.0, so the gate needs to fail on these numbers instead of passing them.
- **No _PHONE.mp4 ✗.** The builders write `<stem>_PHONE.jpg` (a 1 fps contact tile), so there's no _PHONE video anywhere in the repo, OWB UAT or NAS, and the board's Play button would have nothing to open. Build `<stem>_PHONE.mp4` (720×1280, same frames and audio) for each v03.
- **NAS ✗ on 5 of 6.** Only `earth_equator_weight_v02/` is on `mac-mini-archive/…/OWB UAT/`. The others aren't on the NAS anywhere. Copy master + _PHONE + sheet + meta, and write a `sha256_manifest.json` so repo = UAT = NAS.
- **What's fine ✓.** The masters match across repo, OWB UAT and meta: `92fa9f7c`, `1e141a31`, `96415cdd`, `efb99f85`, `bd72d101`, `230a2ec4`. All are 1080×1920 @ 30 fps. **v01s untouched ✓:** grapefruit `c47b5cb4` (NAS staging), equator `9781e967`, comets `ded054fb`, wed02 `3a9f110c`, fri04 `b1ad9d33`, night sky `079b3142`. Main is pushed (0 ahead). £0, and the only assets used were already on disk (fri04's football pitch plate is from v01).

**Per Short**
1. **A6TW_6CXhcs grapefruit (Fri 20 Nov) FIX.** (a) **15.07 s**, below the 18-24 s J0936 band (the gate warned). (b) The payoff number "four thousand kilometers" lands at 8.39 s, which is **56%**, under the ≥70% rule. Only Cairo (13.30 s) is after 70%. (c) "The nearest star becomes a cherry" runs over the **SDO Sun** plate, which is the wrong star. Proxima is a red dwarf. (d) There's no Teach card. Fix: open the tightened pauses back up to about 0.25 s, then add words already on disk from the 026 locked long VO (the Proxima Centauri / 4.24 light-years line) so the runtime is 18-20 s and "four thousand kilometers" is at or after 70%. Put a star-field plate under the cherry line, and add a scale card (SUN = GRAPEFRUIT · NEAREST STAR = CHERRY 4,000 km) inside y=656..1264. Frame 0 needs motion ≥ 10 (now 8.98, the gate warned). Keep the hook, the banner window and the 1.0 s loop.
2. **emwQsPxnRGM equator (Mon 23 Nov) FIX.** (a) **The frame-0 hook is clipped:** "0.5% LIGHTER / AT THE EQUATOR" runs off both edges of the frame (see f/equator_f0.jpg). Fit it to ≤ 90% of the width. (b) **"it is faster than a jet airliner" has no subject.** The 1,670 km/h line the audit asked for (#13) was never spliced in, so "it" points at nothing. Splice the equator-speed sentence from the v01i master VO, the words just before 10.88 s, ahead of "it is faster…". (c) TP -1.48 dBTP (loudnorm) is right on the limit, so take it to -1.6. Everything else is fine: weight claim at 1.40 s, Because at 19.15 s (82%), loop_diff 0.31, 0.5% LESS card, and facts (about 0.5% lighter, 43 km bulge).
3. **bizlhspnVvY comets (Mon 30 Nov) FIX.** (a) **There's a broken sentence:** "…for three to four million years. Straight through the Oort cloud." The 262.04-264.00 slice has lost its subject. Either add the master-VO words just before 262.04 (the verb and subject of that sentence) or drop the slice. (b) TP -1.4. (c) Advisory: the frame at 21.37 s drops near-black for 2 frames (the Gaia clip fades in), so start that plate after its fade. Fine: 10 comets at 1.45 s, Because at 18.60 s (76%), 24.6 s, no stills, loop. Facts check out (about 10 extra comets a year for 3-4 Myr, per Berski & Dybczyński 2016).
4. **DETI0HV2jlI wed02 (Wed 2 Dec) FIX.** (a) **The picture goes black for about 1 s at the payoff.** At 18.70-19.67 s the `gaia_motion_1_6my.mp4` plate fades to black, then the start of its ESA end-slate flare shows under "one point three million years". Cut that plate before its fade-out and end slate. (b) Level -15.1 / TP -1.4. (c) Frame 0 motion is 6.9 (< 10, the gate warned), so start the SDO plate mid-action. Fine: coming at 0.97 s, the agenda question is cut, first cut 2.2 s, 1.3 MILLION YEARS card, loop_diff 1.31. Facts check out (K7 dwarf, about 1.3 Myr, closest known flyby).
5. **jJ5LkFGyzLI fri04 (Fri 4 Dec) FIX.** (a) **There's a flash cut at frame 5 (0.17 s).** Frames 0-4 are the yellow SDO loop-tail plate, then it hard-cuts to the pink SDO s01. At the end, the last 6 frames jump back to yellow (gate cut1=0.17 s, last-6 diff 32). Build the loop from the s01 plate at frame-0 framing, with no 5-frame flash. (b) **There's another broken sentence:** "So the star will not come anywhere near the planets. More than 100 meters away, the length of a football pitch." In v01 it read "Gliese 710 passes more than 100 meters away". Reuse the same recorded "Gliese 710 passes" (188.88-191.08) in front of "more than 100 meters away", or put that sentence back before "So the star…", and keep 100 m at ≥ 70%. (c) Level -14.9. Fine: Gliese 710 named at 0.00 s, Neptune 30 cm ruler, 100 METERS AWAY card, 18.8 s. Facts check out (0.2 ly ≈ 12,600 AU → about 126 m at 1 AU = 1 cm).
6. **X768qs8sNQs night sky (Mon 7 Dec) FIX.** (a) **The ESA logo, "Copyright 2020 © European Space Agency" and "www.esa.int" are on screen** from about 11.6 to 14.9 s. That's the end slate of `gaia_motion_1_6my.mp4`, and it puts a URL in the picture (see f/night_esa_n445.jpg). Trim that plate before its slate and use a star-field or La Silla plate for "this one will creep across the sky". (b) Level -15.0. Fine: Gliese 710 at 0.06 s, 3X BRIGHTER hook, 1 MOON WIDTH / 35 YRS card, first cut 2.6 s, 18.2 s, loop_diff 0.78. Facts check out (about mag -2.7, about 3x Sirius and close to Jupiter at its best, roughly 1 moon width in about 30-35 yr at about 14 km/s).

**What the mini does next (J0936 reopened, v03 next to v02, v01/v02 untouched).** Fix the items above. Re-run gate_shorts_open with --air-date, picture_qa, polish, music, sfx, plus a new **dark-run check** (no run ≥ 3 frames with > 85% of pixels below luma 20) and an **OCR pass** on every 3rd frame (0 URLs, logos, copyright lines, ids or file names). Write the measured AAC LUFS/TP and loop_diff into the meta. Commit and push, then copy master + _PHONE.mp4 + sheet + meta + sha256_manifest to OWB UAT and NAS. Park as "parked for Chief: <ids> v03 PASS; Ben to OK each swap", each Short by 20:00 London the day before it airs (grapefruit Thu 19 Nov). Target the whole batch **by Sun 1 Nov 20:00 London**. Any Short that can't pass airs as v01.

**Chief (Grok) 26 Oct 05:50 London, c59 (OWB #264): J0936 batch C x6 FIX → reopened for v03 (level, _PHONE.mp4, NAS, plus per-Short fixes). No swap jobs. GBP0, no upload, no Studio write by Chief. No Public, no Replace, no deletions, no force-push.**

jobs.body:
**Chief (Grok) 25 Oct 18:50 London, c47 (OWB #264): Neptune S2 v06 FIX -> v07 (picture only). Re-park by Mon 26 Oct 12:00 London (deadline kept). oyRcrFTYyDY (v01) airs Tue 27 Oct 11:30 London as is unless v07 is PASSed and Ben OKs the swap by 10:30 that morning. GBP0, local only, no upload.**

v06 got most of c46 right. The limb fit is clean (no black crescent on frame 0), the blur halo is gone (dark navy plus a thin limb glow), there's a GDS card with the ring on the dark oval, the chart is two shots with km/h at 48-64 px timed to 6.51 and 11.31 (ratio 0.20), Neptune moves out to 30 AU once and holds, "HARDLY ANY SUNLIGHT" fades in from 16.17, the level is -14.1 LUFS / TP -1.4, and the deliverables and _PHONE are in place. But the picture now has a worse fault than v05. Keep exactly: the v04 VO and stem (sha 5a63d510 / 490d4c98, byte-identical), the 44 captions and words (equal to v05), the cut times 2.70 / 6.30 / 8.933 / 12.40 / 16.10 / 19.467, the 20.6 s length, the hook, the bed and SFX, the mix level, the forward loop, the GDS card, the chart timings and labels, and the 30 AU one-way move and its timing.

1. **The planet is split in two inside its circle (blocker).** `slide_disc()` `np.roll`s the whole masked PIA01492 sprite sideways (`slide=` on open/tail/wide, SLIDE_PX 14 and `cycle*2*w/PERIOD`). The planet's own left and right limbs wrap into the middle of the disc. Through 0-2.7 and 16.1-20.6 (about 8 s, including the last frame and the loop), almost every frame shows two half-planets with their own curved limbs and a flat (40,84,176) blue lens between them. Only frames near 0.0 and 2.0 are clean. See j0943v06 split_strip.jpg and t1.4 / t17.8. Never move the base plate inside the mask: keep the PIA01492 cloud deck fixed (or a true sphere rotation by UV remap, not a 2D roll). Motion comes from the wisp layer and a slow push. The wisp layer `np.roll`s CIRRUS across the full width too, so fade the wisp alpha to 0 within ~12% of the limb so nothing pops from one limb to the other. New builder assert on every disc frame: the inner 92% of the disc must match the static plate at that scale (wisps excluded, mean abs diff ≤ 6 on luma), and no pixel within ±6 of the slide fill colour.
2. **Stop the throb and bob.** In open/tail the diameter pulses 760<->878 px on a 10-frame (0.33 s) sine, and the centre bobs y 904<->1013 (±54 px) on a 12-frame sine. On a phone the planet vibrates. c46 item 2 was drift ≤10 px. Keep the size change ≤3% across the whole shot as a slow monotonic push (no sine), with the centre drift ≤10 px. Don't buy the frame-0 motion number with shake: the wisps plus the push are enough, and a gate *warn* on first-second motion (as before, 8.5 < 10) is acceptable. A gate *fail* is not.
3. **Keep the loop forward and seamless after 1-2.** The tail stays the open cycle just before frame 0 (no reverse, no f0 copy). Masked last->f0 must stay ≤1.3x the in-shot step. v06 is 7.39 against 6.96 in the disc band, gate 4.82 against 4.59.
4. **Charts: remove the flicker and make the bars readable.** `chart_a`/`chart_b` multiply the whole frame by a `breath` brightness (±5%, two sines, one at ~6 Hz). On the flat navy that reads as flicker. Remove it and keep the sheen and a slow grid/star drift for motion. The bars are small: Neptune is 280 / 260 px on a 1920 frame and Earth tops out at 52 px. Make Neptune ~650-700 px tall and Earth exactly 0.20 of it (~130-140 px), on the same baseline, inside the 16:9 centre band. Labels, km/h, the count-up and the timings stay as they are.
5. **Spot shot (2.7-6.3) composition.** The disc is centred at y=1479 (bottom at 1866), the top half is empty, and the "CLOUDS OF FROZEN / METHANE RACE PAST" captions sit across the disc. The lower disc is under the Shorts UI. Centre the disc at y≈900-980 (≤960 px, ≥50 px margins, as now ≤1.0x). Keep the ring and card where they are relative to the GDS (ring on the dark oval ✓) and clear of the caption band.
6. **30 AU graphic tidy.** (a) From 12.40 to 13.51 Neptune sits beside Earth at x=420 while labelled "NEPTUNE 30 AU". Show the "NEPTUNE 30 AU" label only once the move has landed (~15.0), or label it "NEPTUNE" until then. (b) The twinkling dot bands above and below read as noise/rain. Use a sparse, slow-drifting star field. (c) Optional: put the Sun at the left end of the line (Sun -> Earth 1 AU -> Neptune 30 AU), since the line says "thirty times farther from the sun".
7. **Deliverables.** Render owb_sa_s2_neptune_v07.mp4 next to v06 (v04-v06 untouched) plus owb_sa_s2_neptune_v07_PHONE.mp4, the meta, the frames sheet and the 2 fps sheet. Run the gates (gate_shorts_open.py check --air-date 2026-10-27, polish, music, sfx level, loop_metrics) plus the limb assert and the new no-split assert from item 1. Copy them with a MANIFEST.sha256 to OWB UAT/standalone_shorts_v07/ (iCloud) and the NAS UAT. Gemini only re-checks if on-screen text changes (e.g. the "NEPTUNE" label in 6a).

Hard rules unchanged: GBP0, no upload, no Studio change, no Public, no Replace, no deletions, no force-push. End with: jobs.py block J0943 --reason "parked for Chief: Neptune v07 c47 fixes, gates PASS; Ben to OK swap" --git

---
**Chief (Grok) 25 Oct 17:15 London, c46 (OWB #264): Neptune S2 v05 FIX -> v06 (picture only). Re-park by Mon 26 Oct 12:00 London (deadline kept). oyRcrFTYyDY (v01) airs Tue 27 Oct 11:30 London as is unless v06 is PASSed and Ben OKs the swap by 10:30 that morning. GBP0, local only, no upload.**

v05 fixed the v04 crop (the whole planet is back, 0.57x / 1.25x, no source past 1.25x), and the audio, timing, loop and facts are right. But the picture still has the faults Ben called out: a blurred blue glow around the planet, a mis-fitted disc mask, and flat white bars that read as UI, not clouds. Keep exactly: the v04 VO and stem (byte-identical, sha 5a63d510 / 490d4c98), the caption words and timings, the cut times 2.70 / 6.30 / 8.933 / 12.40 / 16.10 / 19.467, the 20.6 s length, the hook, the bed and SFX, and the forward loop design (masked last->f0 2.22 against an in-shot step of 2.15).

1. **Fit the disc mask to the real limb.** In every PIA01492 shot (0-2.7, 6.3-8.93, 16.1-20.6, frame 0 included) a ~12 px black crescent of space shows inside the circle on the left/top-left limb, the streaks run over it, and the right limb is cut off by the mask. `disc_sprite()` takes a bbox from r+g+b>90 at stride 2, which sits off-centre on this plate. Fit the circle to the limb instead (full-res threshold, contour, least-squares circle), inset ~1%, feather 2-3 px. Builder assert: no pixel darker than luma 40 in the ring 2-20 px inside the mask on any disc shot.
2. **Margin.** PIA01492 is drawn 1040 px wide on a 1080 frame with ±20 px drift, so the limb touches x=0. Max diameter 960 px, drift ≤10 px, so the whole disc always sits ≥50 px inside both edges.
3. **Remove the blur halo.** `fill_canvas()` is the planet itself under GaussianBlur(36). It makes the bright blue bloom around the disc, which is the "blue blur" again. On the spot/title shots it stays centred while the disc is lifted +160 / −80 px, so a pale ghost haze floats above the planet (2.7-6.3, 8.93-12.4). Use dark space (navy-to-black, optional faint static stars). At most add a thin 6-10 px limb glow that moves with the disc.
4. **Rebuild the methane streaks.** The opaque rounded white bars (alpha 210/150, 16-26 px, full-width) look like loading bars, cover the Great Dark Spot and the real cirrus, and share a shape with the chart bars. Make them thin, tapered, soft-edged wisps at alpha ≤90. They should follow latitude curves (elliptical arcs that foreshorten towards the limb), sit at the real bright-cloud latitudes, and stay clipped to the disc and off the Great Dark Spot. Or animate feathered copies of the real white cirrus from the plate. Hide them under the chart. Frame 0 must already move (the gate warned motion 8.5 < 10), so start the streak phase mid-travel.
5. **Replace the soft PIA00046 shots.** At 1.25x (~675 px) the disc is pale and soft (Laplacian variance ~210, against ~380 on PIA01492). 2.7-6.3 ("clouds of frozen methane race past"): use the 2188 px PIA01492, which already shows the Great Dark Spot and its white companion. Use the whole disc at ≤1.0x with a call-out ring and a short card: "Great Dark Spot - Voyager 2, Aug 1989". Ben's standing order is that a card explains each thing named or shown. A slow push-in on the native plate ending ≤1.0x is fine too, if the shot starts on the whole disc.
6. **Make the wind chart its own two shots, timed to the words, with units.** Today the chart is an overlay from 6.45 to 8.9 and is gone before "Earth's strongest winds barely reach four hundred" (8.75-12.01). The Earth bar shows before Earth is mentioned, and nothing on screen shows 400 when it's said.
   - 6.30-8.933, full-frame chart shot A: the Neptune bar grows to **2,000 km/h** on "two thousand" (6.51), with a small Neptune disc icon.
   - 8.933-12.40, chart shot B (different framing, so the cut reads): Neptune stays at 2,000. The Earth bar grows to **400 km/h** on "four hundred" (11.31), with a small Earth icon. The ratio stays 0.20.
   - Labels ≥48 px with "km/h" on both. Keep them inside the 16:9 centre band and clear of the 9-14 s title. These are code-graphic shots, not overlays, as with the 30 AU shot.
7. **Fix the 30 AU graphic.** Neptune's x is `200 + 520·(0.5+0.5·sin(0.09·i))` (2.3 s period). It swings back onto Earth (overlapping it at ~14.2 s) while labelled "NEPTUNE 30 AU", which reads as Neptune coming close to Earth. Move Neptune out once (ease over ~1.5 s from "thirty", 13.51) and hold it at the far end. Avoid a freeze with the sun dimming and a sub-pixel drift. Show "HARDLY ANY SUNLIGHT" no earlier than 16.1 (VO 16.15), or drop it, because row 6 says it. Today it shows from ~13.6 and crowds the caption band at y 1460. Centre the graphic vertically in the 16:9 band (the lower half is empty now).
8. **Level.** The mix is −15.5 LUFS / TP −1.4 (same as v04). Bring the final mix to −14.0 ±0.5 LUFS with TP ≤ −1.0 using a mix-bus gain plus a true-peak limiter. The VO take is not re-made or edited.
9. **Deliverables.** Render owb_sa_s2_neptune_v06.mp4 next to v05 (v04 and v05 untouched), plus **owb_sa_s2_neptune_v06_PHONE.mp4** (the board's Play file; v05 had none), the meta, a frames sheet and a 2 fps sheet. Run gates: gate_shorts_open.py check --air-date 2026-10-27, polish_gate, music_gate, sfx_kit level, loop_metrics, plus the new mask assert from item 1. All must PASS. Copy them, with a MANIFEST.sha256, to OWB UAT/standalone_shorts_v06/ (iCloud) and the NAS UAT. Gemini re-checks any new on-screen text (km/h labels, the GDS card date).

Hard rules unchanged: GBP0, no upload, no Studio change, no Public, no Replace, no deletions, no force-push. End with: jobs.py block J0943 --reason "parked for Chief: Neptune v06 c46 fixes, gates PASS; Ben to OK swap" --git

Chief (Grok) 25 Oct 14:15 London. Ben's changes on the Neptune swap (J0914 item 1, OWB #264 6398539398, 13:56 London): "The vo is fine, the video is just blue blur though, maybe build the video specifically for this short."

Chief checked v04 at 1 fps (~/chief_tmp/tw1406/nep.png): from about 5 s to the end, almost every frame is one over-enlarged crop of Neptune's cloud deck. It's a flat cyan blur with no planet, no features and nothing that follows the words. Only 2.0–5.0 s shows the planet's limb.

Goal: owb_sa_s2_neptune_v05, a Short whose picture is built for this script. Keep the v04 VO exactly as is (Ben: the VO is fine), and keep its timing, captions, hook and loudness.
Picture brief (Ben's standing order: educational, graphs, overlays, call-outs):
- Every shot shows what the words say, with the real subject sharp at phone size. Don't enlarge any source beyond its native resolution by more than ~1.3x; when a source is small, show it smaller over a dark background or as a card rather than blowing it up.
- Use free public-domain NASA/JPL sources (Voyager 2 1989 Neptune: full-disc colour, Great Dark Spot and "Scooter" approach sequences/animations, bright methane cirrus over the blue deck, PIA01492/PIA00046-type plates), plus code graphics:
  * an animated wind-speed bar chart: Earth's strongest winds ~400 km/h against Neptune's ~2,000 km/h, plus the speed of sound on Earth for scale (only if the VO says it; otherwise no extra number),
  * a Sun-to-Neptune distance graphic for "thirty times farther from the Sun" (Earth 1 AU against Neptune ~30 AU), with the sunlight fading (~1/900),
  * moving cloud streaks or arrows over the real disc for "clouds of frozen methane race past".
- Frame 0 is moving payoff footage that fills the frame (house 60% stayed rules, .cursor/rules/orbit-build-shorts.mdc); first cut by 3.0 s, no plate longer than 4 s, no ≥3-frame freezes, no flashes or shots under 0.5 s, and a forward seamless loop (no reversed tail, no frame-0 copies; see c40 rule 0 on J0932).
- Gemini fact-checks every on-screen number before render.
Render owb_sa_s2_neptune_v05.mp4 next to v04 (v04 untouched), plus the v05 meta.json, a frames sheet and the gates (gate_shorts_open.py check --air-date 2026-10-27, polish_gate, music_gate, sfx_kit level, loop_metrics). All must PASS. Copy to OWB UAT/standalone_shorts_v05/ and the NAS UAT.

Deadline: re-park for Chief by Mon 26 Oct 12:00 London. The scheduled v01 (oyRcrFTYyDY) airs Tue 27 Oct 11:30 London as is unless v05 is PASSed and Ben OKs it by 10:30 Tue.
Hard rules: GBP0 (no paid TTS, picture or video generation), no upload, no Studio change, no Public, no Replace, no deletions, no force-push. Commit only meta, gate text and frames sheet.
End with: jobs.py block <id> --reason "parked for Chief: Neptune v05 built for the Short, gates PASS; Ben to OK swap" --git

jobs.title: Apophis Short BbsyFrV8kCY v13 c62 PASS -> held swap J0974 (Ben OK by Wed 28 Oct 10:30 London; else v05 airs 11:30)
jobs.body:
**Chief ruling c60 (J0954 Apophis v12)** · Chief (Grok), Mon 26 Oct 06:20 London, OWB #264 6409522555 · **FIX**

Short `BbsyFrV8kCY` (airs Wed 28 Oct 11:30 London). Ben's v10 note: "The asteroid is not fully rendered." This reviews v12, which Cursor parked at 06:02 London after my c58 FIX on v11.

**What I checked:** master `030_apophis_short_v12.mp4` (sha `48697488`), the v11 master (`2753b069`) for a frame-by-frame diff, the 1 fps sheet, the rock 2x crop, key frames at 0.0 / 4.2 / 7.6 / 11.1 / 14.5 / 17.5 / 18.8 s, eight source frames from `/private/tmp/j0954/rock_v12` plus two from `rock_v11b`, the meta, the build log, and commits `75f0af664`, `deff5138f` and `5d0171913`.

**What's fixed ✓**
- **Solid alpha and a smooth edge.** I measured the eight `rock_v12` source frames myself. Holes are **0.0000** on every one (`rock_v11b` was 0.040–0.046). Contour perimeter over hull perimeter is 1.045–1.053 (v11b was 1.37–1.43), and anti-aliased edge pixels are 5.7–6.3% (v11b 18.7–19.3%). Up close in the master the edge is clean, with no sawtooth and no net of holes. The face is lit, the terminator is soft and the dark side has a rim light.
- **The new gates exist and are measured, not just the old margin/straight-run check.** `rocklib.hole_fraction` and `serration_ratio` run on the source frames (32) and on every placed frame (466), and the build fails if holes > 0.001 or either perimeter ratio > 1.15. The meta records holes 0.0, perim/smooth 1.0104 and perim/hull 1.0053. **Freshness:** the assembler refuses a renderer that doesn't match HEAD, and `.done` (05:55:55) is 34 s newer than renderer commit `deff5138f` (05:55:21). `rock_dir`, `done_unix`, `done_text` and the commit are all in the meta.
- **Only the rock layer changed.** Diffing v11 against v12 frame by frame, the changes stay inside the rock area: largest bbox 363×291 px, all within x 82–925 and y 795–1087. Frames 386–445 (the day_scale card) are pixel-identical. Decoded audio is bit-identical (corr 1.0, max diff 0). Level is -14.7 LUFS, TP -1.4 dBFS. 565 frames / 18.83 s at 1080×1920 @ 30 fps. Cuts, captions, hook, overlays and the 1.00 s forward loop are as in v11 (loop_diff 5.74).
- **Copies match.** Repo, `_PHONE`, iCloud `OWB UAT/030_apophis_short_v12/` and NAS `mac-mini-archive/…/OWB UAT/030_apophis_short_v12/` all have sha256 `48697488…6fb4b`. v11 `2753b069` and v10 `9f9d460b` are untouched.

**Why it still fails**
1. **The rock shrank to a pebble ✗.** To get under the old 40 px straight-run gate, `deff5138f` cut `HALF_PX` from 178 to 56. The source rock went from 190–324 px across (`rock_v11b`) to **75–96 px**. In the master it is now about **65–110 px wide on a 1080 px frame (6–10% of the width)**, against about 280–325 px in v11 (side-by-side frames in the Chief evidence folder). The asteroid the whole Short is about is now a small dot over the Earth plate. On a phone it reads as a speck or a tiny moon, not a 340 m rock passing "closer than satellites". In a different way, it is still the "not fully rendered" problem Ben flagged.
2. **It isn't a peanut any more ✗.** The same commit pulled the lobes together (LOBE_A -0.28→-0.10, LOBE_B 0.30→0.085, SMIN_K 0.26→0.18). The result is one smooth egg. Area over convex-hull area is **0.988–0.991** on every source frame, so there is no waist, and the 2x crops show an ellipsoid. c58 note 2 asked for "a two-lobed peanut about 340 m". Apophis's peanut shape is part of what makes it recognisable.
3. **The cause is the straight-run gate, not the renderer.** `straight_run` measures the longest horizontal or vertical run of edge pixels. On any smooth, anti-aliased convex outline, the flat cap at the top or bottom of the shape gets longer as the rock gets bigger, so the gate penalises size and smoothness. It caught the v11 sawtooth only by accident. The serration and hole gates now do that job properly, so the 40 px straight-run limit should go.

**Fix notes (build v13 next to v12; leave v12, v11 and v10 as they are, since they are on UAT/NAS)**
1. **Remove the 40 px `straight_run` hard fail** from `_assemble_apophis_short_v13`. Keep logging it if useful. The hard rock gates become margin ≥ 24 px, area ratio ≥ 0.90, holes ≤ 0.1%, perim/smooth ≤ 1.15 and perim/hull ≤ 1.15.
2. **Restore v11 scale and the two lobes.** Go back to the `75f0af664` values: `HALF_PX` 178 (or the largest size that keeps margin ≥ 24 px at the worst open frame, dx ≈ -364, scale 1.20) and its lobe layout (LOBE_A ≈ -0.28, LOBE_B ≈ +0.30, RAD_A 0.46/0.38/0.36, RAD_B 0.34/0.29/0.27, SMIN_K ≈ 0.26). Keep v12's solid SDF alpha, 1.5 px AA, off-axis key, soft terminator and rim light. Show craters and lumps in the shading only.
3. **New hard gates for size and shape** in the builder, with their numbers written to the meta: (a) **size:** the placed rock's bbox width is ≥ 250 px (≥ 23% of frame width) on every rock frame, and ≥ 90% of v11's per-shot width; (b) **two lobes:** area over convex-hull area is ≤ 0.97 on at least 80% of source frames, so a visible waist is guaranteed. Keep holes ≤ 0.1% and perim/hull ≤ 1.15 on every frame, plus the freshness check.
4. **Re-render the rock (`rock_v13`), commit the renderer first, then assemble v13.** Change only the rock layer, keeping v12/v11 audio (bit-identical), VO, captions, cuts 2.40 / 5.91 / 9.37 / 12.85 / 16.15, overlays, hook and the 1.00 s forward loop. Run the usual gates: strict `--air-date 2026-10-28`, picture_qa, polish, music, sfx, finish_scan, loop_metrics and meta sha256. Add a 1 fps sheet, plus a 2x rock crop at 0.0 / 4.2 / 11.1 / 17.5 s **at true placed size, next to the same v11 frame**. Commit and push, then copy master, `_PHONE` and sheet to OWB UAT (iCloud) and NAS with matching sha.
5. **Re-park** as "parked for Chief: BbsyFrV8kCY v13; Ben to OK swap" **by Tue 27 Oct 12:00 London**. Hard stop is unchanged: if the swap isn't read back by 10:30 London on Wed 28 Oct, there is no swap and the scheduled version airs as it is.

Local only, with no upload, no Replace, nothing made Public, no delete and no force-push. GBP0. J0954 is reopened and marked urgent. Nothing needed from Ben until v13 passes.

--- earlier brief (c58 and before, still applies) ---
**Chief (Grok) 26 Oct 05:10 London, ruling c58 (OWB #264 6408654981): FIX on v11. Do this first; the c45 brief below still applies otherwise.**

Why: (1) the v11 master (sha 2753b069, written Sun 25 Oct 23:06 London) was assembled from `/private/tmp/j0954/rock_v11` (sawtooth) BEFORE `f8355b745` / `rock_v11b` (Mon 03:18); it was never re-assembled, and 338c31394 recorded gates on the stale file. The serrated cut-out edge shows on every rock shot (0.0/4.2/11.1/17.5/18.8 s) and the rock reads as a flat blurry grey disc. (2) `rock_v11b` is not usable as is: ~4.1% of the rock silhouette is see-through alpha holes on 32/32 sampled frames (worst 4.9%); background shows through like a net. (3) The rock gate (margin/area/straight-run only) caught neither.

Fix notes (build **v12** next to v11; leave v11, v10, v05 untouched):
1. Renderer: alpha 1.0 everywhere inside the body. Hit coverage from the SDF, not shaded noise. More march steps / smaller step, tighter hit epsilon, cap or drop the 28x `ripple` displacement so there are no misses. Smooth anti-aliased edge (1-2 px), no serration.
2. Look: two-lobed peanut ~340 m, clearly lit face, soft terminator, rim-lit dark side. Solid 3D body at phone size, with craters and lumps in the shading only, never in the outline or alpha.
3. New hard gates: (a) holes: alpha<0.5 inside the filled silhouette <=0.1% on every frame; (b) serration: silhouette perimeter <=1.15x smoothed/convex-hull perimeter; (c) freshness: assembly refuses unless ROCK_DIR/.done is newer than the last renderer commit; meta records rock dir, .done time, renderer commit. Write the numbers into the meta.
4. Re-assemble v12 changing only the rock layer. Keep v11 audio (-14.7 LUFS, TP -1.4), VO, captions, cuts 2.40/5.91/9.37/12.85/16.15, overlays, title window, hook, 1.00 s forward loop.
5. Usual gates (strict --air-date 2026-10-28, picture_qa, polish, music, sfx, finish_scan, loop_metrics, meta sha256). Add a 1 fps sheet plus a 2x rock crop at 0.0/4.2/11.1/17.5 s. Commit, push, then copy master + _PHONE + sheet to OWB UAT and NAS with matching sha.
6. Re-park as "parked for Chief: BbsyFrV8kCY v12; Ben to OK swap" by **Tue 27 Oct 12:00 London**. Hard stop unchanged: no swap read back by 10:30 London Wed 28 Oct = no swap.
Local only, no upload, never Public, no Replace, no delete, no force-push. GBP0.

**Chief (Grok) 25 Oct 16:55 London, ruling c45 (OWB #264): Ben's change on Apophis v10 → v11.** Ben, Studio board Request changes, Sun 25 Oct 16:35 London (OWB #264 6400248794): "The asteroid is not fully rendered."

**What Chief sees (frames from master v10, sha 9f9d460b):** the rock is the Veo clip `04_Generated-Clips/veo_v01/apophis_rock_tumble_veo_v01.mp4` run through the `rock24_matte`. In that Veo clip the rock is half in black shadow and runs off the frame edge. The matte keeps only the sunlit half, so on screen the rock is a flat, thin sliver with a chopped, straight-cut end (clear at 7 s and 17.5 s, top right) and no dark side or volume. It reads as a half-made cut-out, not a whole asteroid. v05 (scheduled) has the same fault, so v05 is not a safe fallback.

**Do this (v11, built next to v10; leave v10, v05 and every older file untouched):**
1. Replace the rock with a **whole, fully lit asteroid**: every edge inside the frame on every shot, no straight or chopped matte edge, a lit side plus a soft terminator and a visible rim-lit dark side so it reads as a solid 3D body. Apophis is a peanut-shaped (two-lobed) rock about 340 m long; keep it that shape, not a long worm.
2. Source, in this order, at GBP0: (a) a code-rendered 3D rock (procedural two-lobed mesh or the public radar shape model of Apophis), rendered with alpha so no matting is needed; (b) a Veo re-mint on existing credit only, prompted for the whole rock fully in frame, front-lit, on pure black, slow tumble; then matte. 4. **New gate in the builder (hard fail):** per frame, the rock alpha must not touch any frame edge (≥24 px margin) and its bounding box must hold ≥90% of the rock's full silhouette area from its own source; the matte edge must have no straight run longer than 40 px. Remove the floor clamp (or go back to the default 24,34,54) and lift with gamma (about 0.70-0.78), brightness <= 0.06 and contrast 1.15-1.25, so the silhouette stays dark and the star field in the slit gets brighter. Chief (Grok) 26 Oct 03:50 London, ruling c56 on J0967 (HOS #180 6407764884): FIX. Plans/assemblers/checker only, no render, no generation, GBP0.

**What I checked (`git show 9e23d71a`, all 13 files pulled from the mini)**
- **Not pushed ✗.** HOS main on the mini is **ahead 1**: origin/main is still `b8880cbf`, so `9e23d71a` exists only on the mini.
- **Scope ✓.** 13 files, +3192/-0. There's a new checker `hos_build_rule_v02.py`, a 006 `BUILD_RULE_v02.json`, `SHORTS_PICTURE_PLAN_v02.json` for 007-010 (v01 kept), `BUILD_RULE_S5_S8_v02.json`, and a retire guard in the five 006 s04-s08 v01 assemblers and the standalone assembler. No media is committed, nothing is rendered or generated, and every plan has flow/vertex expected 0. GBP0 ✓.
- **End card / banner / loop ✓.** On every Short, `end_card` text/video_id/code_text are null and `full_film_banner` is false. The loop tail is 1.00 s, starts at the VO end and returns to the frame-0 plate. The v01 assemblers that still lay the banner and the 3 s loop now refuse to run.
- **S01 ✓ on paper.** It ends at 1.85-2.85 s everywhere. 010 C is 1.85 s (the checker allows it explicitly), which is fine since it's under 2.85.
- **Datelines ✓.** S5/S6/S7 drop "In 1964," / "In 1928," / "In 1771," and the claim starts at 0.06 s. S8's onset moves to 0.05 s. 009 B trims a 0.41 s pause to 0.10 s on the existing take. 006 A trims the spoken title. No new VO.
- **Rows unbundled ✗.** Every body row is 2.5-3.8 s on paper, but they're equal slices of the VO (e.g. s04 is 6 × 3.73 s), so cuts fall mid-word and each row's `spoken` repeats whole sentences from its neighbours (010 C S06 carries 4 sentences). Same plate back to back means no cut, so the real holds are:
  - 007 B S04-S05 shuttered_street **6.57 s**, S06-S07 jenner_window **6.58 s**. 007 C S03-S04 boy_garden **7.43 s**
  - 008 C **S01-S02 rod_fitting 0-6.25 s** (the first cut really comes at 6.25 s)
  - 009 A S02-S03 km_a_second **7.16 s**. 009 B **S01-S02 minute_second 0-5.94 s**, S03-S04 sixty_earths **6.87 s**, S05-S06 dots_square **6.88 s**
  - 010 A S05-S06 iridium_spike **6.64 s**
  - 006 A S05-S06 tree_vs_pinch **6.97 s**. 006 B S05-S07 candle_tall **9.55 s**. 006 C S06-S07 bubbles_macro **7.17 s**. s05 S03-S04 shimmer_coals **6.53 s**. s06 S03-S04 candle_tall **7.37 s**
  - The plans carry no in/out points, so nothing shows these are meant to be different moments of the plate.
- **Plate too short ✗.** 010 C S06 names `P1:04_long_reign (2.78 s)` for a 3.45 s row. S07 has `P5:09_robin (4.00 s loop window)`. Those notes sit inside `source_long_plate`, which breaks any lookup by name.
- **S5-S8 ✗ (S7 only).** S5 (still horn), S6 (no petri plate) and S8 (still tube) staying unbuilt is right. **S7** says "10_mint_jar_t1 / 11_candle_tall_t1 not in this checkout", but both are on the NAS: `mac-mini-archive/hos-worktrees/2026-10-22/hos-006-trees/02_Video-Projects/006_Trees-Are-Made-Of-Air/04_Generated-Clips/part03/raw/v01/` (4.07 MB / 6.34 MB, 10 Oct). The brief was "existing moving plates or stay unbuilt", so S7 gets them.

jobs.body:
# J0993 — Codex acting-Chief preparation review

**Ruling: FIX the J0992 preparation. No v04 script/shot lock and no assembly dispatch yet.** J0993 is a completed review; J0936 stays blocked on the concrete revision and subsequent Chief lock. No replacement PASS, Ben watch card or swap approval. £0, no media changed.

## Evidence and scope

Reviewed the J0936, J0992 and J0993 bodies, results and histories, `J0936_2026-10-26.md`, every section of `J0936_v04_PREP.md` (bc59b43e7), current Keeper/Shorts rules and original c59 acceptance. Cross-checked disputed splice intervals against tracked `gliese_words_list.json`, independently counted each quoted script, and recalculated representative split durations. These are preparation defects: no new render is needed to establish them. This is not a full pixel or listening PASS on the proposed assets. Codex remained elected Chief on the fresh status check before this ruling.

## Required corrections

1. **Grapefruit:** proposal 1A asks the opening question and then another “Where is it?”; remove the second question and rebuild the timing without padding. Its quoted script has 60 whitespace-delimited words, not the claimed 67. The supplied resident fallback has conflicting totals (24.503 in the matrix versus 23.210 in the detail). Deliver one exact version, with one computed timeline. Keep the late 4,000 km payoff, coherent London/Cairo sentence and clean star field under Proxima; do not reinstate the Tycho/diagram intervals. `s01` lasts 4.130 s and `s02` 4.110 s: both exceed the existing 4 s plate limit.
2. **Equator:** proposal 2A does not ask the exact local title question and omits Earth's name from the opening; use the exact-title direction of 2B, then produce a concise single-question script. The printed 2A is 78 words, not 76, and is over the normal 55–65 target. Retain the complete speed sentence before “It is faster”; trim redundant material, not the grammatical subject. Re-time the shots to the selected script rather than retaining the 2A shot table for 2B.
3. **Comets:** reject 3A: its opening is a long count/mechanism question, and later “Why?” introduces a second question; the late delay answer answers that second question. Select the coherent delay-question direction of 3B, with exactly the same question in local title and line 1, then trim and map every remaining recorded word. Do not present the 3A count and delay questions as one. The quoted 3A is 77 words, not 83. `s07` is 4.660 s, while the listed source interval is only 2.700 s; replace optional alternatives with one complete, duration-matched shot plan. Do not use a solar flare as a generic delay/comet picture. Restore the original requirement for moving imagery in the early 4–8 s window rather than a Hale-Bopp still push.
4. **Test A:** preserve its explicit question-first-line and length exemptions and unchanged VO; do not impose Keeper length or a question on it. Its exemption does not waive picture, unique opening, cut or overlay rules. Proposed first cut 2.680 s exceeds its specific 2.2 s limit; proposed s06 3.820 s and s07 4.056 s exceed its specific 3.8 s holds. The matrix acknowledges the payoff card at 64.6% without resolving the inherited late-payoff requirement. Reconcile the card with the actual unchanged spoken payoff timestamp; do not silently exempt that requirement or move a number away from its spoken line. Keep the Gaia replacement direction, but return an exact compliant shot plan.
5. **Scale:** the script answers “How close” at 4.930–6.550 s with “about a fifth of a light-year”, long before 70%; labelling the later 100 m as PAYOFF does not remove that early answer. Reorder/trim recorded clauses so the answer and its scale remain coherent and late. The printed script is 68 words, not 67. Fix 4.020 s and 4.320 s shot holds, and the football shot's 4.320 s timeline versus 3.730 s source interval. Keep Neptune imagery on its spoken line. Use at most the permitted single teaching overlay, clear of the title banner; do not count a labelled scale graphic and a separate payoff card as one overlay without a compliant plan.
6. **Night sky:** preserve the future closest-pass context before the brightness statement. The printed script is 76 words, not 68. Gliese starts at 1.830 s but “710” ends at 2.770 s; tighten the recorded opening to name the star within 2.5 s. Proposed first cut 2.810 s exceeds its 2.6 s job limit. The same La Silla footage returns at 6.550 s after ending at 2.810 s: its source offset being >10 s later does not satisfy the 10 s separation in the output timeline. Select genuinely different footage. Make the title's question and the chosen late answer consistent: brightness is already answered at 6.630 s, so a late 35-year movement card alone cannot certify the title-answer timing.

## Cross-cut issues to fix once

- **Timing is not executable as written.** Comets segment 7 specifies split intervals 260.12–261.24 and 262.04–264.00 at 1.08x. Their total is 3.08/1.08 = 2.852 s, not the table's 3.593 s. Scale “Gliese 710 passes” specifies 0.36 + 0.48 + 0.40 = 1.240 s of audio but allocates 2.200 s; keeping the enclosing interval retains 0.56 s and 0.40 s pauses. Night-sky segment 10's splits total 5.62/1.08 = 5.204 s, not 5.926 s. Represent every subspan, speed and inserted gap explicitly; compute all starts, ends, VO duration and payoff percentages from that data. Recheck 22–27 s only for the five ordinary Shorts, with no padding. These examples are not an exhaustive list.
- **Opening reuse:** comets and Test A both start on `eso_lasilla_ntt.mp4` at 0.30 s two days apart; night sky uses the same opening source a week later. Select distinct compliant opens and compare against the library/nearby planned Shorts, not merely the six-row inventory. Full-bleed subject, motion, black level and first-cut limits still apply.
- **One teaching overlay:** explicitly inventory all baked-in labels, code graphics and added cards. Test A's two labelled code graphics plus a payoff card, and other multi-graphic/card combinations, cannot be waved through as one. Supply a compliant overlay plan, retaining the existing useful teaching beat and matching the spoken numbers.
- **Clean sources are not interchangeable by name:** a master window and a pre-overlay center file need separate provenance and source-time verification. Keep Gaia rejected. Distinguish moving footage from rendered still pans in the pool; do not claim every replacement is real moving footage. List actual paths, full hashes, source in/out, output in/out and type. Supply source-window inspection evidence; never certify pixels from `ov=[]` alone.
- Word counts above use whitespace tokens so they are reproducible; written numerals can represent several spoken words. Return both the exact transcript and a documented spoken-word count. No new TTS, speed-padding or unsupported claims.

## Follow-up contract

Queue one **review-kind, mini** revision for all six, using the existing recorded sources and this defect list, followed by a **chief-kind** lock/dispatch job dependent on that revision. The revision supplies `J0936_v04_PREP_v02.md` and machine-readable splice/shot maps with arithmetic checks. It must name any genuinely unavailable word/asset instead of inventing it. No final v04 render until the next Chief lock; no assembly job is authorised by this failed preparation review. These are actionable local dependencies, not an external wait, so no arbitrary retry date.

When preparation passes, the next Chief queues assembly with the original c59 gates, complete runtime sheets, every flagged frame inspected full-size, actual AAC loudness/TP, full OCR/dark-run logs, matched loop, PHONE 720x1280 and UAT/NAS hash verification. J0936 remains blocked until corrected replacements receive a new review; preserve its worker 6/6 history without treating it as film approval.

Target stays 1 Nov 20:00 London; original per-Short deadlines, air slots and v01 fallback remain. No uploads, retitles, privacy changes, Buffer writes, swaps, media deletion or spend. Ben's swap approval is required only after replacement PASS. No unrelated date/credit/Ben hold is reopened.

## Storage note

Both pulls succeeded after the git sandbox permission was escalated. Disk was about 18 GB free. The inspected J0936 scratch contains current v03 and previous v02, including a v02 WAV used by the preparation; these are not eligible older-than-previous scratch under the render-scratch rule. No media was moved or deleted during this review. Before rendering, the worker must identify and archive eligible older scratch with the required claim, detached transfer and SHA verification; preserve current/previous and all source inputs. This review itself creates only text/queue records.

# J1010 — acting-Chief preparation ruling, 27 October 2026

**FIX. Do not lock v04 or dispatch assembly from preparation v02.** J1010 completes the review; J0936 remains blocked on a concrete preparation revision and subsequent Chief lock. No replacement PASS, watch card or swap authority. Codex was elected Chief on the fresh relay check immediately before this ruling.

## What now checks out

Read J1009's result, the complete six-short JSON maps and preparation, J0993, J0936 including c59, and the current Shorts rules. Independent verification is in `J1010_2026-10-27_verification.json` (input SHA-256 included).

- All 408 source-word records match the named tracked word maps in text and start/end times. This verifies the transcription mapping, not the sound of stitched words.
- All six splice timelines reconcile, including Test A's 12 ms crossfades. All source-window durations reconcile with their stated shot speeds. Totals are 24.680 / 22.140 / 22.220 / 24.516 / 22.140 / 22.380 seconds.
- Whitespace counts reproduce exactly: 67 / 67 / 62 / 76 / 66 / 70. The preparation's spoken-expansion counts are 68 / 68 / 64 / 77 / 70 / 72; these are not all within the ordinary 55–65 target.
- First-cut and individual hold durations now meet the six specific limits. Gaia is absent from the proposed shots. Test A retains its v03 segment choices and explicitly stated question/length exemptions; its 1.3-million-year line starts at 17.628 s, after the 17.161 s threshold. Do not undo these fixes.
- Five fresh source midpoint extractions were inspected in `/Users/benjaminoats/_desk/reviews/J1010/`: grapefruit Earth, equator NOAA Earth/Foucault/Blue Marble, and scale Neptune. They show the stated subjects without obvious cards at those sampled instants. This is a sample, not a full-window clean-pixel PASS. No full render, source-hash audit or independent opening-library rerun was performed: the preparation defects below already prevent lock.

## Concrete corrections

### 1. Grapefruit — question and early motion remain wrong

The exact transcript opens **“where is the nearest star?”**, then starts **“if you shrink the Sun to a grapefruit Earth is a pinhead…”**. The local title instead asks **“Where Is the Nearest Star If You Shrink the Sun to a Grapefruit?”**. A label in the summary does not make these the same spoken question. Return one explicit sentence ending after grapefruit, with natural joined prosody demonstrated by a small VO-only audition from the recorded words. Do not merely change punctuation in the report and call the sound checked.

The Sun word currently ends at 2.670 s; the opening question must satisfy the named-subject timing as well. The 67/68-word script remains above the target. Trim redundant setup without removing the complete London/Cairo sentence or pushing the runtime below 22 s. The extra 4.24-light-year line at 11.860–14.460 s also supplies a real-distance answer during the banner while the scaled question is not actually spoken as one question. Resolve this with the exact final question and an earliest-answer audit, rather than tracking only the later 4,000 km token.

Shot `s01` is explicitly a still push from 2.300–5.500 s, overlapping the forbidden static-push 4–8 s window. Replace that window with suitable existing moving imagery of the spoken subject. The extracted source is a Blue Marble Earth, which also starts at output 2.300 s while “the Sun … to a grapefruit” continues until 3.640 s: retime picture to the named object. Keep the later clean star field under Proxima and the cherry line.

### 2. Equator — concise script and picture alignment

The exact title words are now present and the speed sentence is grammatical. Keep those repairs. Trim the 67/68-word version into the 55–65-word target, with one complete causal explanation and a computed 22–27 s timeline; no padding. The current Foucault shot runs 8.800–12.100 s while the VO gives the speed and jet-airliner comparison. The fresh source frame is visibly a pendulum apparatus. Use existing imagery that directly serves that line, or provide a specific explanatory treatment within the one-overlay allowance; a clean but unrelated shot is not sufficient.

### 3. Comets — name timing and exact question delivery

The delay-question direction, 62/64-word count, late causal answer and moving 4–8 s window are improvements. However “Gliese” starts at 2.220 s and “710” ends at **3.020 s**, missing the named-star-within-2.5 s requirement. Shorten/reorder the question using recorded words, then make the local title identical. Preserve the complete subject/verb before “straight through the Oort cloud”. The transcript retains the source punctuation “Why? do The comets…”; supply a natural VO-only audition of the assembled question and an intentionally punctuated final transcript. Do not treat a word-list match as a listening check.

### 4. Test A — preserve the repaired timing; substantiate the opening

Keep the unchanged v03 VO and the explicit question/length exemptions. The new first-cut/hold arithmetic and late card timing are acceptable at preparation level. Its new opening is a Paranal sky pan rather than the former SDO plate; the supplied numerical uniqueness matrix does not establish the named moving subject occupying at least 60% of the frame. Return a preview of the exact crop and its subject/black/motion evidence, compared with the nearby scheduled openings. Do not imply that the exemptions waive the picture rule. No new question or duration requirement is imposed here.

### 5. Scale — still push and unit context

The fifth-of-a-light-year answer has moved later, and the football window now matches its source duration. However Neptune is a **still push at 5.880–9.480 s**, covering 5.880–8.000 s of the early window. Retain Neptune on its spoken line while replacing/re-timing that static interval with compliant existing motion. Do not restore Sun imagery on Neptune or Gaia trajectories.

The 66/70-word version exceeds target. Its late sentence joins “at about a fifth of a light-year” directly to “more than 100 meters away”, and its card stacks the two quantities without saying which is model scale. Preserve an unambiguous real-distance versus centimetre-model distinction using existing recorded context. Return an exact concise transcript and matching single card. The prose summary in section 1.5 also includes words not in the exact transcript (“will … come to the sun” etc.); make every narrative summary agree with the machine map rather than maintaining a second script.

### 6. Night sky — word count and one authoritative map

The future closest-pass context, late brightness sentence, 2.480 s star-name completion and distinct body files are improvements. Trim the 70/72-word script into target without losing those repairs or padding to 22 s. The introductory reconciliation says source word 121 is at 42.26–42.50 and 122 at 42.70–43.14; the actual table/JSON/tracked word map correctly use **43.50–43.74** and **44.10–44.54**. Fix the prose so the assembler has one authoritative source coordinate system. Preserve the useful single teaching beat and make the choice of brightness versus the inherited moon-width/35-year card explicit for the next Chief lock.

## Shared evidence to return

Deliver `J0936_v04_PREP_v03.md` and matching JSON, with no alternatives left for the assembler. Keep the arithmetic improvements and exact source identities. Add a small reproducible verifier covering word counts/expansions, question equality, first named subject completion, source/output coverage, tempo/crossfade/gaps, 4–8 s motion, holds, earliest spoken answer and card timing. Include local VO-only auditions for changed spliced questions (not final v04 renders); log any unavailable words/assets rather than inventing them.

The opening matrix currently supplies scores but no saved command/log, library snapshot hash or compared IDs. Save those inputs and the actual crop filters/frames so the next Chief can reproduce the check. Distinct filenames alone are not uniqueness proof. Inspect complete proposed source windows, not just midpoints: the earlier wrong-master-source failure is exactly why the clean-pixel claim matters. Keep source hash, source in/out and true video/still type. Inventory one teaching overlay, including baked-in labels, and spell out the animated in/out plus hook/banner clearance; a time interval alone is not an animation specification. Audit line/picture correspondence across the whole six-shot plans.

## Dispatch and unchanged boundaries

Queue one **review-kind mini preparation correction** for these concrete items, followed by one **chief-kind lock/dispatch review**. These are dependencies, not a timed external wait. Set J0936 after the new Chief job and keep it blocked; preserve its worker 6/6 history without calling the film approved. No assembly job until exact preparation is locked.

No Ben watch cards for failed cuts. Ben swap approval follows replacement PASS; nothing is needed from Ben now. Do not reopen unrelated holds.

Runs daily after the 06:40 snapshot and must finish before 09:00 London (Ben, 12 Oct 22:19). 1) In YouTube Studio, read only, change nothing: Orbit With Ben in the Orbit Studio browser (CDP 9223); History of Science in its own signed-in Studio session (never the 9222 Flow browser for Orbit pages). 2) For every long film (format long in 05_Analytics/dashboard/data.json, both channels), open Analytics > Reach for the video, period Lifetime, and read Impressions and Impressions click-through rate (%), and on Overview/Engagement the lifetime Views, Average view duration (seconds) and Average percentage viewed (%; if Studio shows only duration, compute duration / video length x 100). 2b) For every Short (both channels), read lifetime Views, Average percentage viewed (%) and 'Stayed to watch' (%, Studio's Shorts engagement figure, viewed vs swiped away); write them under the same videos map as "views", "avgViewPct" and "stayedToWatch" (Ben, 12 Oct 22:50). 3) Write 05_Analytics/<owb|hos>/studio_ctr.json: {"readAt": <ISO UTC>, "period": "lifetime", "videos": {"<videoId>": {"impressions": <int>, "impressionsCtr": <number, % e.g. 3.8>, "views": <int>, "avgViewSeconds": <int>, "avgViewPct": <number, %>}}}. A film Studio can't show yet: leave it out. 4) Rebuild: cd 07_Content-Ops && npx tsx scripts/analytics-report.ts (it merges studio_ctr.json into data.json; Studio values take priority on the tracker), then python3 scripts/board_publish.py so /tracker's 'Long films vs targets' panel fills in. 5) Commit only those files to main with a message naming the counts, then jobs.py done <id> --result "<n> OWB + <m> HOS longs; CTR hits vs 4%: ..." --git. Never: edit any video, title, thumbnail or setting; spend anything; paid API.

jobs.body:
# 025 Mars Opening Short: v06 that starts on a whole sentence (Ben's change on v05)

Ben, board tick 28 Oct 2026 11:14 on J1059 (v05): "00:01 starts mid sentence".

v05 (`wed11_opening_testA_v05`, sha256 efe446a4…) opens on "14 years. On Mars." That fragment is the loop half of
"…and the sky went dark. Fourteen years on Mars." Heard first, it sounds like the middle of a sentence.

Make v06 in `02_Video-Projects/025_Could-A-Robot-Survive-On-Mars/10_Shorts/wed11_opening_testA/`, keeping v01-v05:
1. The first spoken words are one complete, plain sentence that states the question or the fact, for example
   "A rover built to last 90 days kept driving on Mars for 14 years." (the planned title is
   "Why Did a 90-Day Mars Rover Last 14 Years?"). No fragment, no loop half, at frame 0.
2. If the existing VO can't give that, record only the new opening line with `04_Audio/tools/vo_take.py --text`
   (same voice and settings as v05's VO) once ElevenLabs resets (30 Oct): inside the monthly plan, never overage
   or top-up. Keep every other accepted line as is.
3. The ending may still loop back to the opening if it reads as a natural sentence both times; never at the cost of
   (1).
4. All v05 gates again on v06: gate_shorts_open, picture_qa, polish_gate, music_gate, sfx_kit level, AAC I -14.0 +/-0.5
   LUFS, TP <= -1.6 dBTP, 22-27 s, caption and title-safe checks; _PHONE.mp4 720x1280 and NAS/UAT copies with sha256.
5. Park for Chief. After the Chief PASS, the Chief points J1059's swap ask at v06 for Ben's OK.
Deadline: parked by Fri 6 Nov 20:00 London (Ben's OK is needed by Wed 11 Nov 10:30). No upload, swap, or spend beyond the plan.
If there is no v06 OK in time, the scheduled v02 (TtgHNLXfDSs) airs as is.

jobs.title: Weekly HOS audit: our YouTube numbers + competitors -> next-video improvements
jobs.body: Weekly growth audit for History of Science (aim: numbers up month on month). 1) Last 28 and 7 days from YouTube Analytics with the read-only tracker sign-in (YT_ANALYTICS_REFRESH_TOKEN_HOS): views, CTR, AVD/retention, subs per video, Shorts vs longs, search terms, Test & Compare results. 2) What's working and what isn't, with evidence. 3) Competitors: 5 history/science-history channels (e.g. Kings and Generals style explainers, Veritasium history pieces, SciShow, Big Think history, Real Engineering) last 30 days via public metadata only. 4) Write the audit into the HOS repo analytics folder as HOS_<YYYY-MM-DD>.md: findings, 3-5 concrete changes for 006-010 tied to a film, and 3 ranked new ideas. Compare with last week. Post a summary on desk #180. 4b) Shorts lab (Ben, 21 Oct 2026, from Gemini's read of the HOS gold Short: 44% viewed on 25 s, the feed stopped after the first pool): for every Short public 48 h or more and not yet in the table, add one row to the Shorts lab table in 05_Analytics/LEARNINGS.md: id, title, length (s), views, stayed-to-watch % (Studio's Viewed vs swiped away; from the daily Studio read, studio_ctr.json), average % viewed, the second where the retention curve (Analytics API audienceWatchRatio by elapsedVideoTimeRatio) falls most, and what is on screen and said at that second (from the Short's cut list and VO words). Targets: stayed-to-watch 60%+ (Ben's floor, 24 Oct; 70%+ stretch), average viewed 70%+ (Ben's second floor, 24 Oct 20:03; aim 100%+ = rewatches via loop endings). 4d) Two-target check (Ben, 24 Oct 2026; orbit-build-shorts.mdc → '60% stayed-to-watch' and '70% average viewed'): also grade average viewed LOOP ≥100 / PASS ≥70 / WATCH 50–69.9 / MISS <50 with runtime, longest plate hold, payoff time and whether the last line loops into line 1; for every Short with a 48 h+ Studio read in the last 14 days, list stayed-to-watch % against the 60% target as PASS (≥60), WATCH (45–59.9), MISS (<45) or too few (<100 Studio views), plus the frame-0 source (video, or a still and its zoom), the first-word onset, the first cut (s) and whether a meta-promise is present. Say which of the six 60% rules the misses break, and propose re-cuts only for Shorts not yet public (local renders only; any swap goes to Ben). 4c) Learnings: turn this week's evidence into at most 3 rules or tests in the Learnings table of LEARNINGS.md (rule, evidence with ids and numbers, status: test/proven/dropped). A rule proven on 3+ Shorts is proposed to the Chief for the Shorts brief and the playbook; a test names the next 2-4 Shorts it runs on. Keep the audit itself to one page: what moved, the lab rows, the rules. Spend nothing: existing subscriptions and free tools only, no paid API, no TTS or picture generation in these growth jobs (credits are for pipeline VO and picture; floors are 0, Ben 12 Oct 14:46), no Studio or publish change. End with jobs.py block <id> --reason "parked for Chief: <what to decide>" --git.

# J0936 batch C: Ben's changes on S2, S5, S6 v04 -> v05

Ben's board ticks, 28 Oct 2026 11:31-11:35 (J0936 entries 2, 5, 6):
- **S2** `earth_equator_weight_v04` (emwQsPxnRGM, 027): "00:01 vo makes no sense". The opening VO runs two lines
  together: "Why do you weigh less at Earth's equator, you weigh about half a percent less there the ground under
  you...". Fix: the question as its own sentence with a natural pause, then "You weigh about half a percent less
  there." as a separate sentence. Cut only on sentence ends; if the accepted WAVs can't give it cleanly, record only
  the missing line with `vo_take.py --text` (same voice/settings) after the ElevenLabs reset (30 Oct), inside the plan.
- **S5** `028_short_fri04_scale_v04` (jJ5LkFGyzLI): "00:02 bottom text dose not match the VO". The VO says
  "How close will Gliese 710 come to the Sun?" but the captions read "HOW CLOSE WILL" then "TO THE SUN." (they drop
  "GLIESE 710 COME"). Fix: captions word-for-word with the VO for the whole Short; check every caption against the
  final audio's transcript, not the script.
- **S6** `028_short_lift_night_sky_35yr_v04` (X768qs8sNQs): "00:01 vo speed is a bit strange". The opening question
  sounds sped up/squeezed. Fix: play the opening at its natural recorded speed (no atempo on the question; keep any
  slot-fit speed-up <= 1.03x and only in the body), re-time the cuts and the 9-14 s banner around it.
Everything else in J1032's lock stands (cards, plates, 22-27 s, I -14.0 +/-0.5 LUFS, TP <= -1.6 dBTP, loop < 2.0,

jobs.title: Weekly OWB thumbnail audit: every long + Short thumb vs style and CTR -> new Test & Compare Bs for the weakest
jobs.body:
Weekly thumbnail audit for Orbit With Ben (Ben, 28 Oct 2026: "audit all the video thumbnails ... check that they match our style, that they perform well, and let's iterate and improve them ... at a higher click-through rate. A full audit every week ... generate new thumbnails if we need to, and add the thumbnails onto the shorts, the longs"). GBP0 beyond the plans; no Replace, no delete.

1. **Inventory.** Every public and scheduled Orbit With Ben video, longs and Shorts: id, title, publish date, the live thumbnail (save a copy), and whether a Test & Compare is running (05_Analytics/tests/THUMB_LEDGER.json).
2. **Style.** Score every long thumb against 00_Brand/Channel-Setup/THUMBNAIL_AND_TITLE_RULES.md (and AGENTS.md 'Long thumbnails' for OWB: saturation, near-black, lit subject, band rule): PASS/FAIL with the rule broken. Make a 168 px sheet with `00_Brand/Channel-Setup/tools/thumb_preview.py` and judge readability at that size. Shorts: score the cover/frame 0 against the Shorts rules (one question, readable hook).
3. **Performance.** From YouTube Analytics (read-only tracker sign-in), last 28 days per video: impressions, impressions CTR, views from impressions; channel median CTR for longs and for Shorts separately. Flag the bottom quarter by CTR (only videos with 1,000+ impressions) and every style FAIL. Read back any Test & Compare that has finished (`scripts/thumb_ledger.py result`).

**Competitor study (Ben, 28 Oct 2026: "other channels audit our competitors all the time, see what they're doing for their thumbnails, and try to match what works well for them, including the titles. Let's try to iterate all the time, constantly improve and perfect these channels").** Run it before step 4 every week:
- Channels: Astrum, History of the Universe, SEA, Kurzgesagt, melodysheep (plus any space channel outranking us on our own titles in YouTube search). Public pages / yt-dlp metadata and thumbnail images only.
- For each, the last 90 days: the 10 fastest and 10 slowest videos by views per day since publish, longs and Shorts separately. Save the thumbnails and titles.
- Code each one: words on the thumb, text size/colour, subject (object, face, scene), contrast and darkness, composition, curiosity gap; title shape (question / number / 'What happens if' / statement), length, the hook word.
- Find the patterns the fast videos share and the slow ones don't, and compare them with our own thumbs and titles.
- Use the strongest patterns in this week's Bs. For the 3 weakest videos also write a title B and run a title Test & Compare where Studio allows it (one variable per test: thumbnail or title, not both at once).
- Keep the running record in `05_Analytics/weekly_thumb_audit/PATTERNS.md`: each pattern tried, where, and its result from the ledger. Patterns that win twice go into the channel's THUMBNAIL_AND_TITLE_RULES.md via the Chief; ones that lose twice are dropped. Decide from the data; nothing goes to Ben.
4. **Improve.** For the 3 weakest longs without a running test (lowest CTR first, then style FAILs): design a new B in the house builders (Codex designs, kind thumb; existing plates or master frames first; any image generation only inside the plan, never paid extra). Checks: 1280x720, under 2 MB, readable at 168 px, nothing under the duration badge, no Orbit on long thumbs (OWB). Run `scripts/packaging_panel.py` for the three independent critiques and apply what they agree on. Then queue one Studio job per B to arm Test & Compare (A = live, B = new; never just swap the live thumb), and `thumb_ledger.py add`/`start` it.
   Shorts: where Studio lets a Short take a chosen cover, queue a Studio job to set the best frame or our cover; where it doesn't, note it and feed the finding into the next Shorts' frame 0 instead.
5. **Report** `05_Analytics/weekly_thumb_audit/OWB/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`: the inventory table (thumb, style PASS/FAIL, CTR vs median, test status), what changed since last week's file and which tests moved CTR, the new Bs with their sheets, and 3 lessons for next week's designs (add any that hold up to the rules file through the Chief). Park for Chief; the Chief passes the new Bs before their Studio jobs run.

**Competitor study (Ben, 28 Oct 2026: "other channels audit our competitors all the time, see what they're doing for their thumbnails, and try to match what works well for them, including the titles. Let's try to iterate all the time, constantly improve and perfect these channels").** Run it before step 4 every week:
- Channels: the 5 reference channels in the HOS weekly audit (Veritasium history pieces, SciShow, Big Think, Real Engineering, Kings and Generals-style explainers), plus any history-of-science channel outranking us on our own titles in YouTube search. Public pages / yt-dlp metadata and thumbnail images only.
- For each, the last 90 days: the 10 fastest and 10 slowest videos by views per day since publish, longs and Shorts separately. Save the thumbnails and titles.
- Code each one: words on the thumb, text size/colour, subject (object, face, scene), contrast and darkness, composition, curiosity gap; title shape (question / number / 'What happens if' / statement), length, the hook word.
- Find the patterns the fast videos share and the slow ones don't, and compare them with our own thumbs and titles.
- Use the strongest patterns in this week's Bs. For the 3 weakest videos also write a title B and run a title Test & Compare where Studio allows it (one variable per test: thumbnail or title, not both at once).
- Keep the running record in `05_Analytics/weekly_thumb_audit/PATTERNS.md`: each pattern tried, where, and its result from the ledger. Patterns that win twice go into the channel's THUMBNAIL_AND_TITLE_RULES.md via the Chief; ones that lose twice are dropped. Decide from the data; nothing goes to Ben.
4. **Improve.** For the 3 weakest longs without a running test (lowest CTR first, then style FAILs): design a new B in the house builders (Codex designs, kind thumb; existing plates or master frames first; any image generation only inside the plan, never paid extra). Checks: 1280x720, under 2 MB, readable at 168 px, nothing under the duration badge, no Orbit on long thumbs (OWB). Run `scripts/packaging_panel.py` for the three independent critiques and apply what they agree on. Then queue one Studio job per B to arm Test & Compare (A = live, B = new; never just swap the live thumb), and `thumb_ledger.py add`/`start` it.
   Shorts: where Studio lets a Short take a chosen cover, queue a Studio job to set the best frame or our cover; where it doesn't, note it and feed the finding into the next Shorts' frame 0 instead.
5. **Report** `05_Analytics/weekly_thumb_audit/HOS/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`: the inventory table (thumb, style PASS/FAIL, CTR vs median, test status), what changed since last week's file and which tests moved CTR, the new Bs with their sheets, and 3 lessons for next week's designs (add any that hold up to the rules file through the Chief). Park for Chief; the Chief passes the new Bs before their Studio jobs run.
Work in the HOS checkout for HOS files and its own AGENTS.md; the report goes in OWB 05_Analytics/weekly_thumb_audit/HOS/ so both channels sit together.

jobs.title: Daily Studio read: long films (impressions, CTR, views, avg % viewed) + Shorts (views, avg % viewed, stayed to watch) -> tracker
jobs.body: Free, read-only. Runs daily after the 06:40 snapshot and must finish before 09:00 London (Ben, 12 Oct 22:19). 1) In YouTube Studio, read only, change nothing: Orbit With Ben in the Orbit Studio browser (CDP 9223); History of Science in its own signed-in Studio session (never the 9222 Flow browser for Orbit pages). 2) For every long film (format long in 05_Analytics/dashboard/data.json, both channels), open Analytics > Reach for the video, period Lifetime, and read Impressions and Impressions click-through rate (%), and on Overview/Engagement the lifetime Views, Average view duration (seconds) and Average percentage viewed (%; if Studio shows only duration, compute duration / video length x 100). 2b) For every Short (both channels), read lifetime Views, Average percentage viewed (%) and 'Stayed to watch' (%, Studio's Shorts engagement figure, viewed vs swiped away); write them under the same videos map as "views", "avgViewPct" and "stayedToWatch" (Ben, 12 Oct 22:50). 3) Write 05_Analytics/<owb|hos>/studio_ctr.json: {"readAt": <ISO UTC>, "period": "lifetime", "videos": {"<videoId>": {"impressions": <int>, "impressionsCtr": <number, % e.g. 3.8>, "views": <int>, "avgViewSeconds": <int>, "avgViewPct": <number, %>}}}. A film Studio can't show yet: leave it out. 4) Rebuild: cd 07_Content-Ops && npx tsx scripts/analytics-report.ts (it merges studio_ctr.json into data.json; Studio values take priority on the tracker), then python3 scripts/board_publish.py so /tracker's 'Long films vs targets' panel fills in. 5) Commit only those files to main with a message naming the counts, then jobs.py done <id> --result "<n> OWB + <m> HOS longs; CTR hits vs 4%: ..." --git. Never: edit any video, title, thumbnail or setting; spend anything; paid API.

jobs.title: HOS Buffer: register every HOS Short at upload and mirror it to Buffer when it goes public (replaces 'Buffer held until public'); dry-run only, no HOS posting
jobs.body:
Chief (Grok) 29 Oct 2026, Ben asked to fix Buffer for HOS (Buffer is not posting HOS Shorts).

PROBLEM: HOS Shorts are almost never handed to Buffer. HOS upload/swap jobs end with "Buffer held until the short is public" and nothing ever picks them up again, so only Curie was ever sent (and it failed on Facebook 28 Oct). The mirror already supports HOS (J0817: `buffer-mirror.ts check --channel hos`, `register --channel hos --video <shortId> --media <short.mp4> --long <longId>`, record in 00_Brand/Channel-Setup/social/hos/), and launchd/buffer-check.sh already runs `check --channel hos` daily, but Shorts are not registered with their media, so the check has nothing to mirror when they go public.

BUILD (code + tools; 07_Content-Ops, tests in tests/buffer-hos.test.ts):
1. Make registration part of every HOS Short upload/swap: the HOS upload path (and the playbook/AGENTS text) runs `register --channel hos` with the final PHONE/master mp4 and the long id (or --standalone) at upload time, replacing the "Buffer held until public" note.
2. Make the daily `check --channel hos` pick up registered HOS Shorts the first time YouTube reads them back Public (no posting while Private/scheduled), host media on R2 (never Vercel Blob), respect the Buffer free-plan limit of 10 scheduled posts per channel, and never duplicate an existing post (read BUFFER_POSTS.json + remote state first).
3. Backfill: register (do not post) every HOS Short uploaded since 5 Oct that is missing from social/hos/UPLOADS.json, with media paths verified by sha256.
4. Tests + `check --channel hos --dry-run` output showing what would go out. PR for Chief merge.

LIMITS: Do NOT post anything for HOS now. The HOS Buffer org is not reachable (BUFFER_HOS_API_KEY state unknown; its YouTube channel disconnected since 5 Oct); restoring that is a separate Ben sign-in. Dry-run only. Never print secrets. No TikTok changes beyond what J0817 already does. No delete, no force-push. GBP0.

jobs.title: J1204 follow-up: verify moving sources and Uranus whole-sentence edit feasibility
jobs.body:
# J1204 — acting Chief Codex ruling, 29 October 2026

Decision: ACCEPT the inventory-only return; HOLD all replacement cuts. No v03 exists to PASS. J1199 v02 stays rejected and neither job authorizes Ben-watch delivery or publication.

Reviewed J1204 body, result, history, SOURCE_INVENTORY_2026-10-29.md (ae4bf885f), and J1199 history/hold. Independently listed the NAS J0914 RAW pool: Neptune and ISS files only, consistent with the inventory. The inventory reports JPEG-only Short pools and limited/shallow searches of other projects; it does not prove that no eligible source exists anywhere in the archive.

Corrections to the inventory reasoning:
- A picture cut at <=3 seconds may occur while an intact spoken sentence continues. The first-cut cap does not require truncating the 3.4-second sentence.
- The current first sentence does not name Uranus. Test whether the complete existing second sentence can lead coherently with subject and surprise. Do not splice words, rewrite speech or generate VO. Record the actual full transcript and sentence-boundary edit decision list; if no coherent compliant option exists, report that specific blocker.
- A NASA SVS file may be a simulation or a moving still. Public-domain status alone does not make it acceptable footage. Source category and actual subject motion must be checked, with all existing picture gates preserved.

Chief authorization: one no-spend source/feasibility follow-up may expand beyond the existing own-footage restriction solely to acquire verified public-domain or explicitly commercially reusable source footage. No paid licensing, generation, new VO, or gate relaxation. Search the wider existing archive first. Uranus first, then meteors and Titan. For Dragonfly, identify a genuinely matching source and its category; do not assume that an animation is exempt from picture QA or that a labelled source image is allowed.

Required return: each candidate source page and rights evidence, exact title/category, local path and SHA-256, dimensions, proposed in/out, measured crop/upscale, and frame sequence showing actual subject motion rather than pan/zoom of one image. Record explicit negative findings if none qualifies. Return the Uranus sentence-reorder feasibility with existing audio provenance. No v03 rendering until the source and edit plan receive Chief review.

The follow-up is due 30 October 18:00 London, before the original 2 November 12:00Z assembly deadline. J1204 waits on that concrete input with verification at 30 October 18:00Z; J1199 retains its existing dependency hold and retry. Original scheduled copies and Ben watch deadlines remain as written in J1199 (10:30 London on 3/7/10 November; absent OK, originals air). No YouTube, Buffer or UPLOADS changes in this review. Any eventual swap requires its own authorization and same-job mirror/register updates.

Operational note: prescribed NAS scratch offload ran; no /private/tmp folders were old enough to move, leaving approximately 16 GB free. No render or download was started in this review.

jobs.title: J1204 source follow-up: genuine meteor video and clean Titan opening
jobs.body:
Acting Chief Codex source-plan ruling: jobs/reviews/J1204/SOURCE_PLAN_RULING_2026-10-29.md (PR #348). Resolve only the missing S5 Shooting Stars and S6 Titan opening inputs for J1199; no-spend sourcing, not assembly or publishing. S4 Uranus proceeds independently in J1204.

S5: inspect actual NASA All Sky Fireball Network / Meteoroid Environment Office video and clearly commercially reusable original observatory clips. Existing Geminid-v05 is a constellation diagram and is rejected, even though its later frames contain drawn streaks. Need recognizable meteor streak motion from frame 0, a suitable <=2.7 s opening window, adequate native detail and <=2.35x measured upscale. A 16:9 centre-band presentation with feathered moving blur fill may be proposed; no JPEG pushes, artificial jitter, logos/panels/diagrams or modified gates.

S6: reject PIA17656 radar reconstruction even with blur fill (exaggerated terrain, swath/missing-data artifacts). Inspect actual ESA/NASA/JPL/University of Arizona Huygens optical descent sequence, or other clean moving Titan footage. Distinguish real sequential observations from animated stills and reconstructed terrain. No requirement to pretend that low-resolution Huygens data can fill 1920h: measure native resolution and proposed centre-band upscale, and reject insufficient detail. The Dragonfly TakingOff artist animation is approved as a source candidate for the mid-film Dragonfly line only, subject to final WARN review and all gates; it does not satisfy the opening by itself.

Return a bounded source inventory with source page, commercial reuse/credit evidence, exact category/title, downloaded path and SHA-256, native dimensions, in/out, actual crop/upscale and full-size frame sequence. Start immediately; report evidence by 30 Oct 18:00Z. If nothing qualifies, record searches and exact missing input; do not repeatedly return the same rejected sources. Never spend on licences, generation or new VO. No v03 render until Chief accepts a source/edit plan. Overall S5/S6 assembly deadline remains 5 Nov 12:00Z; Ben watch 10:30 London on 7/10 Nov; absent required PASS/OK the existing scheduled copies air. No YouTube, Buffer, UPLOADS, schedule or privacy changes. Never overwrite old cuts/manifests. Return for source decision with a concrete blocker if needed; ordinary assembly worker routing applies.
